12	import com.savie.precut.model.OutputSize
13	import com.savie.precut.model.Project
14	import javax.inject.Inject
15	
16	/** The single Project → Composition path shared by preview and export. */
17	class CompositionBuilder @Inject constructor(private val effectsFactory: EffectsFactory) {
18	
19	    /** Returns null when the project has nothing to play. */
20	    fun build(project: Project): Composition? {
21	        val spec = compositionSpecOf(project)
22	        if (spec.items.isEmpty()) return null
23	        val sequence = EditedMediaItemSequence.Builder(setOf(C.TRACK_TYPE_AUDIO, C.TRACK_TYPE_VIDEO))
24	            .addItems(spec.items.map { toEditedMediaItem(it, spec.outputSize) })
25	            .build()
26	        val builder = Composition.Builder(listOf(sequence) + spec.audioLanes.map(::audioSequence))
27	        effectsFactory.textOverlayEffect(spec.texts, spec.outputSize)?.let { overlay ->
28	            builder.setEffects(Effects(/* audioProcessors= */ emptyList(), /* videoEffects= */ listOf(overlay)))
29	        }
30	        return builder.build()
31	    }
32	
33	    /** One audio row: for each clip, a silent gap up to its start, then the clip. */
34	    private fun audioSequence(lane: List<AudioItemSpec>): EditedMediaItemSequence {
35	        val builder = EditedMediaItemSequence.Builder(setOf(C.TRACK_TYPE_AUDIO))
36	        lane.forEach { audio ->
37	            if (audio.gapBeforeMs > 0) builder.addGap(audio.gapBeforeMs * 1_000)
38	            val mediaItem = MediaItem.Builder()
39	                .setUri(audio.uri)
40	                .setClippingConfiguration(
41	                    MediaItem.ClippingConfiguration.Builder()
42	                        .setStartPositionMs(audio.clipStartMs)
43	                        .setEndPositionMs(audio.clipEndMs)
44	                        .build(),
45	                )
46	                .build()
47	            builder.addItem(
48	                EditedMediaItem.Builder(mediaItem)
49	                    .setDurationUs(audio.sourceDurationMs * 1_000)
50	                    .setEffects(Effects(effectsFactory.audioProcessors(audio.sound), emptyList()))
51	                    .apply { if (audio.speed != 1f) applySpeed(audio.speed, capFrameRate = false) }
52	                    .build(),
53	            )
54	        }
55	        return builder.build()
56	    }
57	
58	    private fun toEditedMediaItem(item: ItemSpec, outputSize: OutputSize): EditedMediaItem {
59	        val audio = if (item is ItemSpec.Video) effectsFactory.audioProcessors(item.sound) else emptyList()
60	        val effects = Effects(audio, effectsFactory.videoEffects(item.visual, outputSize))
61	        return when (item) {
62	            is ItemSpec.Video -> {
63	                val mediaItem = MediaItem.Builder()
64	                    .setUri(item.uri)
65	                    .setClippingConfiguration(
66	                        MediaItem.ClippingConfiguration.Builder()
67	                            .setStartPositionMs(item.clipStartMs)
68	                            .setEndPositionMs(item.clipEndMs)
69	                            .build(),
70	                    )
71	                    .build()
72	                EditedMediaItem.Builder(mediaItem)
73	                    // CompositionPlayer requires the pre-clipping, pre-speed source duration.
74	                    .setDurationUs(item.sourceDurationMs * 1_000)
75	                    .setEffects(effects)
76	                    .apply { if (item.speed != 1f) applySpeed(item.speed) }
77	                    .build()
78	            }
79	            is ItemSpec.Image -> {
80	                val mediaItem = MediaItem.Builder()
81	                    .setUri(item.uri)
82	                    .setImageDurationMs(item.durationMs)
83	                    .build()
84	                EditedMediaItem.Builder(mediaItem)
85	                    .setDurationUs(item.durationMs * 1_000)
86	                    .setFrameRate(IMAGE_FRAME_RATE)
87	                    .setEffects(effects)
88	                    .build()
89	            }
90	        }
91	    }
92	
93	    /**
94	     * Constant speed for preview and export alike, keeping the audio's pitch. Sped-up clips get a
95	     * frame-rate cap so 4x footage doesn't produce a 120+ fps output.
96	     */
97	    @OptIn(ExperimentalApi::class) // SpeedParameters (pitch control) is experimental in Media3 1.11.
98	    private fun EditedMediaItem.Builder.applySpeed(speed: Float, capFrameRate: Boolean = true) {
99	        setSpeed(SpeedParameters(ConstantSpeedProvider(speed), /* shouldMaintainPitch= */ true))
100	        if (capFrameRate && speed > 1f) setFrameRate(MAX_FRAME_RATE)
101	    }
102	
103	    private companion object {
104	        const val IMAGE_FRAME_RATE = 30
105	        const val MAX_FRAME_RATE = 60
106	    }
107	}

@Composable
fun EditorScreen(
    onBack: () -> Unit,
    onExport: (projectId: String) -> Unit,
    viewModel: EditorViewModel = hiltViewModel(),
) {
    val uiState by viewModel.uiState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
    val previewState by viewModel.previewState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
    val canSplit by viewModel.canSplit.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
    val snackbarHostState = remember { SnackbarHostState() }
    val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
    val resources = LocalResources.current

    LifecycleEventEffect(Lifecycle.Event.ON_STOP) { viewModel.onScreenStopped() }

    val picker = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(PickMultipleVisualMedia()) { uris ->
        viewModel.onMediaPicked(uris.map(Uri::toString))
    }
    // OpenDocument (not GetContent) so the music Uri can be kept across restarts.
    val musicPicker = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(OpenDocument()) { uri ->
        viewModel.audio.onMusicPicked(uri?.toString())
    }
    val replacementPicker = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(PickVisualMedia()) { uri ->
        viewModel.onReplacementPicked(uri?.toString())
    }
    val micPermission = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(RequestPermission()) { granted ->
        if (granted) viewModel.audio.onRecordStart(hasPermission = true)
    }
    ObserveAsEvents(viewModel.events) { event ->
        val message = when (event) {

/**

 * main toolbar. Audio-clip panels live in [AudioPanels].
 */
@Composable
fun EditorBottomPanel(state: EditorUiState.Ready, canSplit: Boolean, positionMs: Long, viewModel: EditorViewModel) {
    val context = LocalContext.current
    val recording by viewModel.audio.recording.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
    val clip = state.project.clips.firstOrNull { it.id == state.selectedClipId }
    val text = state.project.textOverlays.firstOrNull { it.id == state.selectedTextId }
    val audio = state.project.audioClips.firstOrNull { it.id == state.selectedAudioId }
    val close = viewModel::onToolClosed

    if (audio != null) {
        AudioPanels(audio, state.activeTool, positionMs, viewModel)
        return
    }
    when {
        state.activeTool == EditorTool.TRIM && clip != null ->
            TrimTool(clip, onTrim = { start, end -> viewModel.onTrim(clip.id, start, end) }, onDone = close)
        state.activeTool == EditorTool.SPEED && clip != null ->
            SpeedTool(clip.speed, onSpeedChanged = viewModel::onSpeedChanged, onDone = close)
        state.activeTool == EditorTool.FILTER && clip != null ->
            FilterTool(clip, viewModel.thumbnails, onFilterSelected = viewModel::onFilterSelected, onDone = close)
        state.activeTool == EditorTool.VOLUME && clip != null ->
            ClipVolumeTool(clip, viewModel::onClipVolumeChanged, viewModel::onClipMutedChanged, onDone = close)
        state.activeTool == EditorTool.FADE && clip != null ->
            FadeTool(clip.fadeInMs, clip.fadeOutMs, clip.timelineDurationMs(), viewModel::onClipFadesChanged, onDone = close)
        state.activeTool == EditorTool.TEXT && text != null ->
            TextTool(text, onChange = viewModel::onTextChanged, onDelete = viewModel::onDeleteText, onDone = close)
        state.activeTool == EditorTool.RATIO ->
            RatioTool(state.project.aspectRatio, onSelected = viewModel::onAspectRatioSelected, onDone = close)
        state.activeTool == EditorTool.VOICEOVER -> VoiceoverTool(
            recording = recording,
            playheadMs = positionMs,
            onRecord = {
                val granted = ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(context, Manifest.permission.RECORD_AUDIO) ==
                    PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
                viewModel.audio.onRecordStart(granted)
            },
            onStop = viewModel.audio::onRecordStop,
            onDone = close,
        )
        state.audioMenuOpen -> AudioMenuBar(
            onBack = { viewModel.onAudioMenu(false) },
            onMusic = viewModel.audio::onAddMusic,
            onExtract = viewModel.audio::onExtract,
            onRecord = { viewModel.onToolSelected(EditorTool.VOICEOVER) },
        )
        else -> MainToolbar(state, canSplit, viewModel)
    }
}

/** Timeline callbacks routed to the ViewModel (and its audio controller). */
@Composable
fun rememberTimelineActions(viewModel: EditorViewModel): TimelineActions = remember(viewModel) {
    object : TimelineActions {
        override fun onScrubStart() = viewModel.onScrubStart()
        override fun onSeek(positionMs: Long) = viewModel.onSeek(positionMs)
        override fun onSelectClip(clipId: String?) = viewModel.onClipSelected(clipId)
        override fun onTrim(clipId: String, trimStartMs: Long, trimEndMs: Long) =
            viewModel.onTrim(clipId, trimStartMs, trimEndMs)

        override fun onSelectText(textId: String) = viewModel.onTextSelected(textId)
        override fun onTextTiming(textId: String, startMs: Long, endMs: Long) =
            viewModel.onTextTimingChanged(textId, startMs, endMs)
        override fun onToggleOriginalAudio() = viewModel.onToggleOriginalAudio()
        override fun onSelectAudio(audioId: String) = viewModel.audio.onSelected(audioId)
        override fun onAudioTiming(audioId: String, timelineStartMs: Long, trimStartMs: Long, trimEndMs: Long) =
            viewModel.audio.onTiming(audioId, timelineStartMs, trimStartMs, trimEndMs)
        override fun onAddAudio() = viewModel.onAudioMenu(true)

}

internal val VerticalPadding = 8.dp
internal val RulerHeight = 18.dp
internal val LaneGap = 6.dp
internal val ClipHeight = 56.dp
private val TextLaneHeight = 22.dp
private val AudioRowHeight = 24.dp

/** Height the timeline needs for the project's audio rows (at least one, for "+ Add audio"). */
fun timelineHeight(project: Project): Dp {
    val rows = project.audioLanes().size.coerceAtLeast(1)
    return VerticalPadding * 2 + RulerHeight + LaneGap + ClipHeight + LaneGap + TextLaneHeight + (LaneGap + AudioRowHeight) * rows
}

/** What's selected on the timeline; at most one of these is set. */
data class TimelineSelection(
    val clipId: String? = null,
    val textId: String? = null,
    val audioId: String? = null,
    /** Items whose media is missing (drawn in red). */
    val missingIds: Set<String> = emptySet(),
)

/** Ruler, clip strip, text lane and audio rows, stacked; laid out in timeline px. */
@Composable
fun TimelineLanes(
    project: Project,
    selection: TimelineSelection,
    pxPerMs: Float,
    visiblePx: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>,
    loader: ThumbnailLoader,
    waveforms: WaveformLoader,
    playheadMs: () -> Long,
    actions: TimelineActions,
) {
    val density = LocalDensity.current
    val totalMs = project.totalDurationMs()
    val contentWidthPx = TimelineGeometry.msToPx(totalMs, pxPerMs)
    val snapThresholdMs = (with(density) { 10.dp.toPx() } / pxPerMs).toLong()
    val snapTargets = snapTargetsOf(project)
    val snap = { ownerId: String, start: Long, end: Long, move: Long ->
        val targets = snapTargets.filter { it.first != ownerId }.map { it.second } + playheadMs()
        TimelineGeometry.snapMove(start, end, move, targets, snapThresholdMs)
    }

    TimelineRuler(
        totalMs = totalMs,
        pxPerMs = pxPerMs,
        modifier = Modifier
            .width(with(density) { contentWidthPx.toDp() })
            .height(RulerHeight),
    )
    Spacer(Modifier.height(LaneGap))
    ClipStrip(
        project = project,
        selectedClipId = selection.clipId,
        missingIds = selection.missingIds,
        pxPerMs = pxPerMs,
        clipHeight = ClipHeight,
        visiblePx = visiblePx,
        loader = loader,
        onTrim = actions::onTrim,
    )
    Spacer(Modifier.height(LaneGap))
    TextLane(
        overlays = project.textOverlays,
        selectedTextId = selection.textId,
        pxPerMs = pxPerMs,
        widthPx = contentWidthPx,
        height = TextLaneHeight,
        snap = snap,
        onSelect = actions::onSelectText,
        onTiming = actions::onTextTiming,
    )
    AudioRows(
        project = project,
        selectedAudioId = selection.audioId,
        videoDurationMs = totalMs,
        pxPerMs = pxPerMs,
        rowHeight = AudioRowHeight,
        rowGap = LaneGap,
        waveforms = waveforms,
        snap = snap,
        actions = actions,
    )
}

/** Edges and beats bars can snap to, tagged with the id of the item they belong to. */
private fun snapTargetsOf(project: Project): List<Pair<String, Long>> = buildList {
    project.clipStartTimesMs().forEach { add("" to it) }

    }
}

import kotlin.math.roundToLong

private val BarShape = RoundedCornerShape(4.dp)

/** Pending drags of a [TimelineBar], in ms: body move and start/end handle deltas. */
data class BarDrag(val moveMs: Long = 0L, val startMs: Long = 0L, val endMs: Long = 0L)

/**
 * A bar on a timeline lane (text, music). Drag the body sideways to move it (selecting it first if
 * needed); the selected bar has start/end handles. Drags show live via [rangeFor] and are reported
 * once on release via [onCommit]. Gestures are keyed on [id] only, so selection changes mid-drag
 * don't restart them.
 */
@Composable
fun TimelineBar(
    id: String,
    label: String,
    color: Color,
    selected: Boolean,
    pxPerMs: Float,
    /** Timeline start/end to draw for the given pending drag. */
    rangeFor: (BarDrag) -> Pair<Long, Long>,
    onSelect: () -> Unit,
    onCommit: (BarDrag) -> Unit,
    /** Adjusts a raw body-move delta (ms) to snap to beats/playhead/edges; identity by default. */
    snapMove: (Long) -> Long = { it },
    decoration: @Composable BoxScope.(startMs: Long, endMs: Long) -> Unit = { _, _ -> },
) {
    val density = LocalDensity.current
    val haptics = LocalHapticFeedback.current
    val currentSelected by rememberUpdatedState(selected)
    val currentPxPerMs by rememberUpdatedState(pxPerMs)
    val currentOnSelect by rememberUpdatedState(onSelect)
    val currentOnCommit by rememberUpdatedState(onCommit)
    val currentSnapMove by rememberUpdatedState(snapMove)

    var moveDragPx by remember { mutableFloatStateOf(0f) }
    var startDragPx by remember { mutableFloatStateOf(0f) }
    var endDragPx by remember { mutableFloatStateOf(0f) }
    var moving by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
    var snapped by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

    fun rawMoveMs() = (moveDragPx / currentPxPerMs).roundToLong()

    fun dragNow() = BarDrag(
        moveMs = rawMoveMs().let { if (it == 0L) 0L else currentSnapMove(it) },
        startMs = (startDragPx / currentPxPerMs).roundToLong(),
        endMs = (endDragPx / currentPxPerMs).roundToLong(),
    )

    fun commit() {
        val drag = dragNow()
        moveDragPx = 0f
        startDragPx = 0f
        endDragPx = 0f
        moving = false
        snapped = false
        if (drag != BarDrag()) currentOnCommit(drag)
    }

    val (start, end) = rangeFor(dragNow())
    Box(
        Modifier
            .offset { IntOffset((start * pxPerMs).roundToInt(), 0) }
            .width(with(density) { ((end - start) * pxPerMs).toDp() })
            .fillMaxHeight()
            .clip(BarShape)
            .background(color)
            .then(if (selected || moving) Modifier.border(1.5.dp, ClipSelection, BarShape) else Modifier)
            .pointerInput(id) { detectTapGestures(onTap = { currentOnSelect() }) }
            .pointerInput(id) {
                detectHorizontalDragGestures(
                    onDragStart = {
                        moving = true
                        haptics.performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackType.GestureThresholdActivate)
                        if (!currentSelected) currentOnSelect()
                    },
                    onDragEnd = { commit() },
                    onDragCancel = { commit() },
                ) { change, amount ->
                    change.consume() // the timeline must not scroll while a bar moves
                    moveDragPx += amount
                    val raw = rawMoveMs()
                    val nowSnapped = currentSnapMove(raw) != raw
                    if (nowSnapped && !snapped) haptics.performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackType.SegmentTick)
                    snapped = nowSnapped
                }
            },
    ) {
        decoration(start, end)
        Text(
            text = if (moving) formatPreciseMs(start) else label,
            style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelSmall,
            maxLines = 1,
            overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis,
            modifier = Modifier
                .align(Alignment.CenterStart)
                .padding(horizontal = if (selected) 16.dp else 6.dp),
        )
        if (selected) {
            TrimHandle(onDrag = { startDragPx += it }, onDragEnd = ::commit, modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterStart))
            TrimHandle(onDrag = { endDragPx += it }, onDragEnd = ::commit, modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterEnd))
        }
    }
}

private val ClipShape = RoundedCornerShape(6.dp)

/**
 * One clip on the strip: thumbnail tiles (only those in [visiblePx], in clip-local px) plus, when
 * selected, a border and trim handles. Handle drags preview locally and call [onTrim] on release.
 */
@Composable
fun ClipView(
    clip: Clip,
    pxPerMs: Float,
    height: Dp,
    selected: Boolean,
    /** Shows the muted badge (clip muted, at 0%, or all original audio muted). */
    soundOff: Boolean,
    /** The media can't be opened: tinted red with a warning mark. */
    missing: Boolean,
    visiblePx: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>,
    loader: ThumbnailLoader,
    onTrim: (trimStartMs: Long, trimEndMs: Long) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
    val density = LocalDensity.current
    // Pending handle drags, in px of timeline; applied as a trim on release.
    var startDragPx by remember(clip.id) { mutableFloatStateOf(0f) }
    var endDragPx by remember(clip.id) { mutableFloatStateOf(0f) }
    fun commitTrim(start: Long, end: Long) {
        startDragPx = 0f
        endDragPx = 0f
        onTrim(start, end)
    }
    val previewTrimStart = (clip.trimStartMs + startDragPx / pxPerMs * clip.speed).roundToLong()
        .coerceIn(0L, clip.trimEndMs)
    val previewTrimEnd = (clip.trimEndMs + endDragPx / pxPerMs * clip.speed).roundToLong()
        .coerceIn(previewTrimStart, clip.sourceDurationMs)
    val shown = clip.copy(trimStartMs = previewTrimStart, trimEndMs = previewTrimEnd)
    val widthPx = TimelineGeometry.msToPx(shown.timelineDurationMs(), pxPerMs)
    val heightPx = with(density) { height.roundToPx() }
    val tileWidthPx = heightPx * TILE_ASPECT

    Box(
        modifier
            .width(with(density) { widthPx.toDp() })
            .height(height)
            .clip(ClipShape)
            .background(ClipBackground),
    ) {
        val times = TimelineGeometry.thumbnailSourceTimesMs(shown, widthPx, tileWidthPx)
        times.forEachIndexed { i, sourceMs ->
            val left = i * tileWidthPx
            if (left + tileWidthPx >= visiblePx.start && left <= visiblePx.endInclusive) {
                ThumbnailTile(
                    loader = loader,
                    key = ThumbnailKey(clip.uri, clip.type, sourceMs, heightPx, clip.sourceRotationDegrees),
                    modifier = Modifier
                        .offset { IntOffset(left.roundToInt(), 0) }
                        .width(with(density) { tileWidthPx.toDp() })
                        .fillMaxHeight(),
                )
            }
        }
        if (missing) {
            Box(
                Modifier
                    .matchParentSize()
                    .background(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error.copy(alpha = 0.55f)),
                contentAlignment = Alignment.Center,
            ) {
                Text("!", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, color = Color.White)
            }
        }
        if (soundOff) {
            Icon(
                painterResource(R.drawable.ic_volume_off),
                contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.volume_muted),
                tint = Color.White,
                modifier = Modifier
                    .align(Alignment.TopStart)
                    .padding(start = 16.dp, top = 3.dp)
                    .size(14.dp)
                    .background(Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.5f), CircleShape),
            )
        }
        if (selected) {
            Box(Modifier.matchParentSize().border(2.dp, ClipSelection, ClipShape))
            TrimHandle(
                onDrag = { startDragPx += it },
                onDragEnd = { commitTrim(previewTrimStart, previewTrimEnd) },
                modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterStart),
            )
            TrimHandle(
                onDrag = { endDragPx += it },
                onDragEnd = { commitTrim(previewTrimStart, previewTrimEnd) },
                modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterEnd),
            )
        }
    }
}

/** Width/height ratio of a thumbnail tile. */
const val TILE_ASPECT = 0.75f
package com.savie.precut.ui.editor.timeline

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.key
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.Dp
import com.savie.precut.media.ThumbnailLoader
import com.savie.precut.model.Project
import com.savie.precut.model.clipStartTimesMs

/** Clips side by side, each as wide as its timeline duration. [visiblePx] is in timeline px. */
@Composable
fun ClipStrip(
    project: Project,
    selectedClipId: String?,
    missingIds: Set<String>,
    pxPerMs: Float,
    clipHeight: Dp,
    visiblePx: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>,
    loader: ThumbnailLoader,
    onTrim: (clipId: String, trimStartMs: Long, trimEndMs: Long) -> Unit,
) {
    Row {
        val starts = project.clipStartTimesMs()
        project.clips.forEachIndexed { index, clip ->
            val clipStartPx = TimelineGeometry.msToPx(starts[index], pxPerMs)
            // key(): after a reorder each clip keeps its own state (drag offsets, tiles).
            key(clip.id) {
                ClipView(
                    clip = clip,
                    pxPerMs = pxPerMs,
                    height = clipHeight,
                    selected = clip.id == selectedClipId,
                    soundOff = clip.muted || clip.volume == 0f || project.originalAudioMuted,
                    missing = clip.id in missingIds,
                    visiblePx = (visiblePx.start - clipStartPx)..(visiblePx.endInclusive - clipStartPx),
                    loader = loader,
                    onTrim = { start, end -> onTrim(clip.id, start, end) },
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

import com.savie.precut.ui.components.formatPreciseMs
import com.savie.precut.ui.theme.ClipSelection
import kotlin.math.roundToInt
import kotlin.math.roundToLong

private val BarShape = RoundedCornerShape(4.dp)

/** Pending drags of a [TimelineBar], in ms: body move and start/end handle deltas. */
data class BarDrag(val moveMs: Long = 0L, val startMs: Long = 0L, val endMs: Long = 0L)

/**
 * A bar on a timeline lane (text, music). Drag the body sideways to move it (selecting it first if
 * needed); the selected bar has start/end handles. Drags show live via [rangeFor] and are reported
 * once on release via [onCommit]. Gestures are keyed on [id] only, so selection changes mid-drag
 * don't restart them.
 */
@Composable
fun TimelineBar(
    id: String,
    label: String,
    color: Color,
    selected: Boolean,
    pxPerMs: Float,
    /** Timeline start/end to draw for the given pending drag. */
    rangeFor: (BarDrag) -> Pair<Long, Long>,
    onSelect: () -> Unit,
    onCommit: (BarDrag) -> Unit,
    /** Adjusts a raw body-move delta (ms) to snap to beats/playhead/edges; identity by default. */
    snapMove: (Long) -> Long = { it },
    decoration: @Composable BoxScope.(startMs: Long, endMs: Long) -> Unit = { _, _ -> },
) {
    val density = LocalDensity.current
    val haptics = LocalHapticFeedback.current
    val currentSelected by rememberUpdatedState(selected)
    val currentPxPerMs by rememberUpdatedState(pxPerMs)
    val currentOnSelect by rememberUpdatedState(onSelect)
    val currentOnCommit by rememberUpdatedState(onCommit)
    val currentSnapMove by rememberUpdatedState(snapMove)

    var moveDragPx by remember { mutableFloatStateOf(0f) }
    var startDragPx by remember { mutableFloatStateOf(0f) }
    var endDragPx by remember { mutableFloatStateOf(0f) }
    var moving by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
    var snapped by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

    fun rawMoveMs() = (moveDragPx / currentPxPerMs).roundToLong()

    fun dragNow() = BarDrag(
        moveMs = rawMoveMs().let { if (it == 0L) 0L else currentSnapMove(it) },
        startMs = (startDragPx / currentPxPerMs).roundToLong(),
        endMs = (endDragPx / currentPxPerMs).roundToLong(),
    )

    fun commit() {
        val drag = dragNow()
        moveDragPx = 0f
        startDragPx = 0f
        endDragPx = 0f
        moving = false
        snapped = false
        if (drag != BarDrag()) currentOnCommit(drag)
    }

    val (start, end) = rangeFor(dragNow())
    Box(
        Modifier
            .offset { IntOffset((start * pxPerMs).roundToInt(), 0) }
            .width(with(density) { ((end - start) * pxPerMs).toDp() })
            .fillMaxHeight()
            .clip(BarShape)
            .background(color)
            .then(if (selected || moving) Modifier.border(1.5.dp, ClipSelection, BarShape) else Modifier)
            .pointerInput(id) { detectTapGestures(onTap = { currentOnSelect() }) }
            .pointerInput(id) {
                detectHorizontalDragGestures(
                    onDragStart = {
                        moving = true
                        haptics.performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackType.GestureThresholdActivate)
                        if (!currentSelected) currentOnSelect()
                    },
                    onDragEnd = { commit() },
                    onDragCancel = { commit() },
                ) { change, amount ->
                    change.consume() // the timeline must not scroll while a bar moves
                    moveDragPx += amount
                    val raw = rawMoveMs()
                    val nowSnapped = currentSnapMove(raw) != raw
                    if (nowSnapped && !snapped) haptics.performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackType.SegmentTick)
                    snapped = nowSnapped
                }
            },
    ) {
        decoration(start, end)
        Text(
            text = if (moving) formatPreciseMs(start) else label,
            style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelSmall,
            maxLines = 1,
            overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis,
            modifier = Modifier
                .align(Alignment.CenterStart)
                .padding(horizontal = if (selected) 16.dp else 6.dp),
        )
        if (selected) {
            TrimHandle(onDrag = { startDragPx += it }, onDragEnd = ::commit, modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterStart))
            TrimHandle(onDrag = { endDragPx += it }, onDragEnd = ::commit, modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterEnd))
        }
    }
}

private val ClipShape = RoundedCornerShape(6.dp)

/**
 * One clip on the strip: thumbnail tiles (only those in [visiblePx], in clip-local px) plus, when
 * selected, a border and trim handles. Handle drags preview locally and call [onTrim] on release.
 */
@Composable
fun ClipView(
    clip: Clip,
    pxPerMs: Float,
    height: Dp,
    selected: Boolean,
    /** Shows the muted badge (clip muted, at 0%, or all original audio muted). */
    soundOff: Boolean,
    /** The media can't be opened: tinted red with a warning mark. */
    missing: Boolean,
    visiblePx: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>,
    loader: ThumbnailLoader,
    onTrim: (trimStartMs: Long, trimEndMs: Long) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
    val density = LocalDensity.current
    // Pending handle drags, in px of timeline; applied as a trim on release.
    var startDragPx by remember(clip.id) { mutableFloatStateOf(0f) }
    var endDragPx by remember(clip.id) { mutableFloatStateOf(0f) }
    fun commitTrim(start: Long, end: Long) {
        startDragPx = 0f
        endDragPx = 0f
        onTrim(start, end)
    }
    val previewTrimStart = (clip.trimStartMs + startDragPx / pxPerMs * clip.speed).roundToLong()
        .coerceIn(0L, clip.trimEndMs)
    val previewTrimEnd = (clip.trimEndMs + endDragPx / pxPerMs * clip.speed).roundToLong()
        .coerceIn(previewTrimStart, clip.sourceDurationMs)
    val shown = clip.copy(trimStartMs = previewTrimStart, trimEndMs = previewTrimEnd)
    val widthPx = TimelineGeometry.msToPx(shown.timelineDurationMs(), pxPerMs)
    val heightPx = with(density) { height.roundToPx() }
    val tileWidthPx = heightPx * TILE_ASPECT

    Box(
        modifier
            .width(with(density) { widthPx.toDp() })
            .height(height)
            .clip(ClipShape)
            .background(ClipBackground),
    ) {
        val times = TimelineGeometry.thumbnailSourceTimesMs(shown, widthPx, tileWidthPx)
        times.forEachIndexed { i, sourceMs ->
            val left = i * tileWidthPx
            if (left + tileWidthPx >= visiblePx.start && left <= visiblePx.endInclusive) {
                ThumbnailTile(
                    loader = loader,
                    key = ThumbnailKey(clip.uri, clip.type, sourceMs, heightPx, clip.sourceRotationDegrees),
                    modifier = Modifier
                        .offset { IntOffset(left.roundToInt(), 0) }
                        .width(with(density) { tileWidthPx.toDp() })
                        .fillMaxHeight(),
                )
            }
        }
        if (missing) {
            Box(
                Modifier
                    .matchParentSize()
                    .background(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error.copy(alpha = 0.55f)),
                contentAlignment = Alignment.Center,
            ) {
                Text("!", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, color = Color.White)
            }
        }
        if (soundOff) {
            Icon(
                painterResource(R.drawable.ic_volume_off),
                contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.volume_muted),
                tint = Color.White,
                modifier = Modifier
                    .align(Alignment.TopStart)
                    .padding(start = 16.dp, top = 3.dp)
                    .size(14.dp)
                    .background(Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.5f), CircleShape),
            )
        }
        if (selected) {
            Box(Modifier.matchParentSize().border(2.dp, ClipSelection, ClipShape))
            TrimHandle(
                onDrag = { startDragPx += it },
                onDragEnd = { commitTrim(previewTrimStart, previewTrimEnd) },
                modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterStart),
            )
            TrimHandle(
                onDrag = { endDragPx += it },
                onDragEnd = { commitTrim(previewTrimStart, previewTrimEnd) },
                modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterEnd),
            )
        }
    }
}

/** Width/height ratio of a thumbnail tile. */
const val TILE_ASPECT = 0.75f
package com.savie.precut.ui.editor.timeline

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.key
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.Dp
import com.savie.precut.media.ThumbnailLoader
import com.savie.precut.model.Project
import com.savie.precut.model.clipStartTimesMs

/** Clips side by side, each as wide as its timeline duration. [visiblePx] is in timeline px. */
@Composable
fun ClipStrip(
    project: Project,
    selectedClipId: String?,
    missingIds: Set<String>,
    pxPerMs: Float,
    clipHeight: Dp,
    visiblePx: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>,
    loader: ThumbnailLoader,
    onTrim: (clipId: String, trimStartMs: Long, trimEndMs: Long) -> Unit,
) {
    Row {
        val starts = project.clipStartTimesMs()
        project.clips.forEachIndexed { index, clip ->
            val clipStartPx = TimelineGeometry.msToPx(starts[index], pxPerMs)
            // key(): after a reorder each clip keeps its own state (drag offsets, tiles).
            key(clip.id) {
                ClipView(
                    clip = clip,
                    pxPerMs = pxPerMs,
                    height = clipHeight,
                    selected = clip.id == selectedClipId,
                    soundOff = clip.muted || clip.volume == 0f || project.originalAudioMuted,
                    missing = clip.id in missingIds,
                    visiblePx = (visiblePx.start - clipStartPx)..(visiblePx.endInclusive - clipStartPx),
                    loader = loader,
                    onTrim = { start, end -> onTrim(clip.id, start, end) },
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

import kotlin.math.min

/**
 * Drag handle for the selected text over the preview. Idle, it outlines where the burned-in text
 * is; while dragging it shows the text itself. Sizes follow the export's rules (TextOverlayRenderer).
 */
@Composable
fun TextPositionOverlay(
    overlay: TextOverlay,
    aspectRatio: AspectRatio,
    onMoved: (xNorm: Float, yNorm: Float) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
    val currentOnMoved by rememberUpdatedState(onMoved)
    BoxWithConstraints(modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
        // The letterboxed video frame inside the preview (ContentScale.Fit), in px.
        val output = outputSizeFor(aspectRatio)
        val boxW = constraints.maxWidth.toFloat()
        val boxH = constraints.maxHeight.toFloat()
        val scale = min(boxW / output.width, boxH / output.height)
        val frameW = output.width * scale
        val frameH = output.height * scale
        val left = (boxW - frameW) / 2
        val top = (boxH - frameH) / 2

        var drag by remember(overlay.id, overlay.xNorm, overlay.yNorm) { mutableStateOf<Offset?>(null) }
        // Read at drag end, so a long-lived gesture never uses stale geometry or position.
        val start by rememberUpdatedState(Offset(overlay.xNorm, overlay.yNorm))
        val frameSize by rememberUpdatedState(Offset(frameW, frameH))
        val centerX = left + overlay.xNorm * frameW + (drag?.x ?: 0f)
        val centerY = top + overlay.yNorm * frameH + (drag?.y ?: 0f)

        val density = LocalDensity.current
        val textPx = textSizePx(overlay.textSizeSp, min(frameW, frameH).roundToInt())
        val padding = with(density) { (textPx * TEXT_PADDING_RATIO).toDp() }
        val shape = RoundedCornerShape(with(density) { (textPx * TEXT_CORNER_RATIO).toDp() })
        val dragging = drag != null
        val background = overlay.backgroundArgb?.takeIf { dragging }?.let(::Color) ?: Color.Transparent

        Text(
            text = overlay.text.ifBlank { stringResource(R.string.text_placeholder) },
            color = if (dragging || overlay.text.isBlank()) Color(overlay.colorArgb).copy(alpha = 0.85f) else Color.Transparent,
            fontSize = with(density) { textPx.toSp() },
            textAlign = TextAlign.Center,
            modifier = Modifier
                .layout { measurable, _ ->
                    val maxWidth = (frameW * 0.9f + 2 * padding.toPx()).roundToInt().coerceAtLeast(1)
                    val placeable = measurable.measure(Constraints(maxWidth = maxWidth))
                    layout(placeable.width, placeable.height) {
                        placeable.place((centerX - placeable.width / 2f).roundToInt(), (centerY - placeable.height / 2f).roundToInt())
                    }
                }
                .pointerInput(overlay.id) {
                    detectDragGestures(
                        onDragStart = { drag = Offset.Zero },
                        onDragEnd = {
                            val moved = drag ?: Offset.Zero
                            drag = null
                            currentOnMoved(
                                (start.x + moved.x / frameSize.x).coerceIn(0f, 1f),
                                (start.y + moved.y / frameSize.y).coerceIn(0f, 1f),
                            )
                        },
                        onDragCancel = { drag = null },
                    ) { change, amount ->
                        change.consume()
                        drag = (drag ?: Offset.Zero) + amount
                    }
                }
                .border(1.dp, Color.White.copy(alpha = 0.9f), shape)
                .background(background, shape)
                .padding(padding),
        )
    }
}
package com.savie.precut.media

import android.graphics.Bitmap
import android.graphics.Canvas
import android.graphics.Paint
import android.graphics.RectF
import android.text.Layout
import android.text.StaticLayout
import android.text.TextPaint
import com.savie.precut.model.OutputSize
import javax.inject.Inject
import kotlin.math.ceil

/**
 * Draws a text overlay into a bitmap at output resolution: centred lines, wrapped at 90% of the
 * frame width, on an optional rounded background. The editor's on-screen ghost mirrors these
 * proportions ([TEXT_PADDING_RATIO], [TEXT_CORNER_RATIO]).
 */
class TextOverlayRenderer @Inject constructor() {

    fun render(spec: TextSpec, outputSize: OutputSize): Bitmap {
        val paint = TextPaint(Paint.ANTI_ALIAS_FLAG).apply {
            textSize = spec.textSizePx
            color = spec.colorArgb
        }
        val maxWidth = (outputSize.width * 0.9f).toInt().coerceAtLeast(1)
        val layout = StaticLayout.Builder.obtain(spec.text, 0, spec.text.length, paint, maxWidth)
            .setAlignment(Layout.Alignment.ALIGN_CENTER)
            .setIncludePad(false)
            .build()
        val textWidth = (0 until layout.lineCount).maxOfOrNull { layout.getLineWidth(it) } ?: 0f
        val padding = spec.textSizePx * TEXT_PADDING_RATIO
        val width = ceil(textWidth + 2 * padding).toInt().coerceAtLeast(1)
        val height = ceil(layout.height + 2 * padding).toInt().coerceAtLeast(1)

        val bitmap = Bitmap.createBitmap(width, height, Bitmap.Config.ARGB_8888)
        val canvas = Canvas(bitmap)
        spec.backgroundArgb?.let { background ->
            val radius = spec.textSizePx * TEXT_CORNER_RATIO
            canvas.drawRoundRect(
                RectF(0f, 0f, width.toFloat(), height.toFloat()),
                radius,
                radius,
                Paint(Paint.ANTI_ALIAS_FLAG).apply { color = background },
            )
        }
        // The layout is maxWidth wide with centred lines; shift it so the text block is centred.
        canvas.translate(padding - (maxWidth - textWidth) / 2f, padding)
        layout.draw(canvas)
        return bitmap
    }
}

const val TEXT_PADDING_RATIO = 0.25f
const val TEXT_CORNER_RATIO = 0.2f
package com.savie.precut.media

import android.graphics.Bitmap
import androidx.annotation.OptIn
import androidx.media3.common.OverlaySettings
import androidx.media3.common.util.UnstableApi
import androidx.media3.effect.BitmapOverlay
import androidx.media3.effect.StaticOverlaySettings

/** A pre-rendered text bitmap, centred on its anchor and visible only within its time range. */
@OptIn(UnstableApi::class)
class TimedTextOverlay(private val spec: TextSpec, private val bitmap: Bitmap) : BitmapOverlay() {

    private val visible: OverlaySettings = StaticOverlaySettings.Builder()
        .setBackgroundFrameAnchor(spec.anchorX, spec.anchorY)
        .build()

    private val hidden: OverlaySettings = StaticOverlaySettings.Builder()
        .setBackgroundFrameAnchor(spec.anchorX, spec.anchorY)
        .setAlphaScale(0f)
        .build()

    override fun getBitmap(presentationTimeUs: Long): Bitmap = bitmap

    override fun getOverlaySettings(presentationTimeUs: Long): OverlaySettings =
        if (spec.isVisibleAt(presentationTimeUs)) visible else hidden
}

                        onDragCancel = { drag = null },
                    ) { change, amount ->
                        change.consume()
                        drag = (drag ?: Offset.Zero) + amount
                    }
                }
                .border(1.dp, Color.White.copy(alpha = 0.9f), shape)
                .background(background, shape)
                .padding(padding),
        )
    }
}
package com.savie.precut.media

import android.graphics.Bitmap
import android.graphics.Canvas
import android.graphics.Paint
import android.graphics.RectF
import android.text.Layout
import android.text.StaticLayout
import android.text.TextPaint
import com.savie.precut.model.OutputSize
import javax.inject.Inject
import kotlin.math.ceil

/**
 * Draws a text overlay into a bitmap at output resolution: centred lines, wrapped at 90% of the
 * frame width, on an optional rounded background. The editor's on-screen ghost mirrors these
 * proportions ([TEXT_PADDING_RATIO], [TEXT_CORNER_RATIO]).
 */
class TextOverlayRenderer @Inject constructor() {

    fun render(spec: TextSpec, outputSize: OutputSize): Bitmap {
        val paint = TextPaint(Paint.ANTI_ALIAS_FLAG).apply {
            textSize = spec.textSizePx
            color = spec.colorArgb
        }
        val maxWidth = (outputSize.width * 0.9f).toInt().coerceAtLeast(1)
        val layout = StaticLayout.Builder.obtain(spec.text, 0, spec.text.length, paint, maxWidth)
            .setAlignment(Layout.Alignment.ALIGN_CENTER)
            .setIncludePad(false)
            .build()
        val textWidth = (0 until layout.lineCount).maxOfOrNull { layout.getLineWidth(it) } ?: 0f
        val padding = spec.textSizePx * TEXT_PADDING_RATIO
        val width = ceil(textWidth + 2 * padding).toInt().coerceAtLeast(1)
        val height = ceil(layout.height + 2 * padding).toInt().coerceAtLeast(1)

        val bitmap = Bitmap.createBitmap(width, height, Bitmap.Config.ARGB_8888)
        val canvas = Canvas(bitmap)
        spec.backgroundArgb?.let { background ->
            val radius = spec.textSizePx * TEXT_CORNER_RATIO
            canvas.drawRoundRect(
                RectF(0f, 0f, width.toFloat(), height.toFloat()),
                radius,
                radius,
                Paint(Paint.ANTI_ALIAS_FLAG).apply { color = background },
            )
        }
        // The layout is maxWidth wide with centred lines; shift it so the text block is centred.
        canvas.translate(padding - (maxWidth - textWidth) / 2f, padding)
        layout.draw(canvas)
        return bitmap
    }
}

const val TEXT_PADDING_RATIO = 0.25f
const val TEXT_CORNER_RATIO = 0.2f
package com.savie.precut.media

import android.graphics.Bitmap
import androidx.annotation.OptIn
import androidx.media3.common.OverlaySettings
import androidx.media3.common.util.UnstableApi
import androidx.media3.effect.BitmapOverlay
import androidx.media3.effect.StaticOverlaySettings

/** A pre-rendered text bitmap, centred on its anchor and visible only within its time range. */
@OptIn(UnstableApi::class)
class TimedTextOverlay(private val spec: TextSpec, private val bitmap: Bitmap) : BitmapOverlay() {

    private val visible: OverlaySettings = StaticOverlaySettings.Builder()
        .setBackgroundFrameAnchor(spec.anchorX, spec.anchorY)
        .build()

    private val hidden: OverlaySettings = StaticOverlaySettings.Builder()
        .setBackgroundFrameAnchor(spec.anchorX, spec.anchorY)
        .setAlphaScale(0f)
        .build()

    override fun getBitmap(presentationTimeUs: Long): Bitmap = bitmap

    override fun getOverlaySettings(presentationTimeUs: Long): OverlaySettings =
        if (spec.isVisibleAt(presentationTimeUs)) visible else hidden
}

entries.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using `find`/Glob, `grep`/Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

You can launch up to 3 agent(s) in parallel.

**Guidelines:**
- **Default**: Launch at least 1 Plan agent for most tasks - it helps validate your understanding and consider alternatives
- **Skip agents**: Only for truly trivial tasks (typo fixes, single-line changes, simple renames)
- **Multiple agents**: Use up to 3 agents for complex tasks that benefit from different perspectives

Examples of when to use multiple agents:

Example perspectives by task type:
- New feature: simplicity vs performance vs maintainability
- Bug fix: root cause vs workaround vs prevention
- Refactoring: minimal change vs clean architecture

1. Read the critical files you identified during exploration to deepen your understanding

3. Use AskUserQuestion to clarify any remaining questions with the user

Goal: Write your final plan to the plan file (the only file you can edit).
- Begin with a **Context** section: explain why this change is being made — the problem or need it addresses, what prompted it, and the intended outcome
- Include only your recommended approach, not all alternatives
- Ensure that the plan file is concise enough to scan quickly, but detailed enough to execute effectively
- Name the critical files to be modified. For changes that repeat a pattern across many files, describe the pattern once and list a few representative paths — do not enumerate every file or line number
- Reference existing functions and utilities you found that should be reused, with their file paths
- Include a verification section describing how to test the changes end-to-end (run the code, use MCP tools, run tests)

### Phase 5: Call ExitPlanMode
At the very end of your turn, once you have asked the user questions and are happy with your final plan file - you should always call ExitPlanMode to indicate to the user that you are done planning.
This is critical - your turn should only end with either using the AskUserQuestion tool OR calling ExitPlanMode. Do not stop unless it's for these 2 reasons

**Important:** Use AskUserQuestion ONLY to clarify requirements or choose between approaches. Use ExitPlanMode to request plan approval. Do NOT ask about plan approval in any other way - no text questions, no AskUserQuestion. Phrases like "Is this plan okay?", "Should I proceed?", "How does this plan look?", "Any changes before we start?", or similar MUST use ExitPlanMode.

NOTE: At any point in time through this workflow you should feel free to ask the user questions or clarifications using the AskUserQuestion tool. Don't make large assumptions about user intent. The goal is to present a well researched plan to the user, and tie any loose ends before implementation begins.

# Phase 7 — Core editing parity (CapCut audit of Phases 1–4)

## Context
Phase 6 is approved and committed (`ae57547`). The per-phase CapCut audit in `docs/PLAN.md` §6 found gaps in what Phases 1–4 built: import and preview, timeline, speed and ratio, and text. Phase 7 closes them before the bigger visual phases start. Everything runs on-device with Media3 1.11.1. I checked the one new Media3 API this phase uses: `StaticOverlaySettings.Builder.setRotationDegrees` exists (counter-clockwise, so it gets negated like clip rotation).

The work is in 6 blocks. I build and test after each one.

## A. Import and preview
1. **Insert at the playhead**
   - Pure `Project.insertIndexAt(timelineMs)` in `model/TimelineMath.kt`. It returns the clip boundary nearest the playhead: before the clip if the playhead is in its first half, after it otherwise, and the end of the list when empty or at the end.
   - `EditorViewModel.onMediaPicked` passes it as `AddClips.atIndex`.
2. **Camera**
   - The editor's `+` becomes a small menu: *Photos & videos* / *Record video* / *Take photo*. Home gets a camera action next to "New project".
   - Uses the `CaptureVideo` / `TakePicture` contracts with a `FileProvider` Uri into `filesDir/captures/<uuid>.mp4|jpg`. Intents don't need the CAMERA permission.
   - The stored clip Uri is `Uri.fromFile(...)`, which is our own file. New `media/CaptureFiles.kt` creates the file and both Uris.
   - Manifest gets a `<provider>`, plus `res/xml/file_paths.xml` covering only `captures/`.
3. **Share to PreCut**
   - `MainActivity` gets intent filters for `ACTION_SEND` / `ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE` with `video/*` and `image/*`, and `launchMode="singleTask"`; `onNewIntent` handles shares too.
   - Shared Uris only have temporary read grants, so new `media/SharedMediaCopier` copies them into `filesDir/imports/` with a progress state. A singleton `ShareInbox` (StateFlow) hands them over.
   - `AppNavHost` pops back to Home, and `HomeViewModel` consumes the inbox: copy, then the existing import path, then a new project, then OpenEditor.
   - `AndroidMediaImporter` skips `takePersistableUriPermission` for `file://` Uris.
4. **Cleanup:** the Phase 6 `VoiceoverJanitor` becomes `AppMediaJanitor`. It sweeps `voiceovers/`, `captures/` and `imports/` for files no project references (same rule: only on the Projects screen).
5. **Full-screen preview**
   - A `fullScreen` flag in `Ready` and a button on `PlaybackControls`.
   - `FullScreenPreview` uses the same player and overlays the whole screen, with a scrub `Slider`, play/pause, time and close. It hides the system bars with `WindowInsetsControllerCompat`, and `BackHandler` closes it.

## B. Timeline
6. **Trim snapping:** `ClipView` handles snap the dragged edge to the playhead and to text/audio edges and beats. They reuse `snapTargetsOf` and `TimelineGeometry.snapMove`'s threshold, with a haptic tick. A new pure `TimelineGeometry.snapEdge(edgeMs, targets, threshold)` does the work. While dragging, the start handle visually follows the finger (the clip's content is offset by the drag), as in CapCut.
7. **Auto-scroll near edges**
   - New `EdgeAutoScroller` (provided by `Timeline` through a CompositionLocal, holding the `ScrollState` and viewport width). While a bar or trim handle drag is within 48dp of the viewport edge, it scrolls with speed proportional to depth. It reports the scrolled px back to the drag so the edge stays under the finger.
   - It's used by `TimelineBar`, `TrimHandle` and `ClipView`.
8. **Frame-level zoom and ruler**
   - `MAX_DP_PER_SECOND` goes from 480 to 1500, about 50dp per frame at 30 fps.
   - New pure `TimelineGeometry.rulerTicks(pxPerMs, minSpacingPx, totalMs)`. Below 100 ms it switches to frame ticks (30 fps, as CapCut uses) labelled `5f`, `10f`…, and seconds stay labelled. `TimelineRuler` draws its output.
9. **Clip badges:**
   - a speed badge (`2.0x`) on any clip whose speed isn't 1
   - the duration (`3.2s`) at the top-left of the selected clip
   - the existing muted badge
   All three go in a small `ClipBadges` composable, so `ClipView` stays under 150 lines.
10. **Multi-select**
    - The main toolbar gets **Select**, which sets `Ready.multiSelect: Set<String>?`; non-null means select mode.
    - In select mode, taps toggle clips, texts and audio clips through the existing `onSelectClip`/`onTextSelected`/`audio.onSelected` routes, checked in the ViewModel. They draw a selected border without handles.
    - The bottom bar becomes `SelectionToolbar`: a count, then *Delete, Duplicate, Speed, Filter, Volume, Done*. Speed, Filter and Volume reuse `SpeedTool`, `FilterTool` and `VolumeSlider`.
    - Undo: a new `EditAction.Batch(actions: List<EditAction>)` folds through the reducer, so a batch is one history step. Speed and Filter skip photos and audio; Volume covers clips and audio.
11. **Apply to all:** a button in `FilterTool` and `ClipVolumeTool` that sends a `Batch` covering every clip.
12. **Project cover**
    - `Project.cover: ProjectCover?`: either `Frame(timelineMs)` or `Image(uri)`. It's chosen with a new **Cover** tool (main toolbar), which offers a frame scrubber over the preview or *From gallery*.
    - `ProjectCoverMaker.keyFor`/`make` use the chosen cover: they find the frame through `clipAt` plus `ThumbnailLoader`, or decode the image.
    - `Project.coverInExport` (a switch in the panel): the composition-level overlay shows the cover full-frame for the first frame only, through a new `CoverOverlay` (a `BitmapOverlay` loaded lazily on the effects thread). Timing stays identical in preview and export.

## C. Speed (clip)
13. **Range and pitch**
    - The range becomes 0.1x–100x: `MIN_SPEED`/`MAX_SPEED` in `EditReducer`.
    - New `Clip.keepPitch = true`, set by a new `SetKeepPitch` action and mapped to `SpeedParameters(..., shouldMaintainPitch)`. Audio-clip speed stays 0.5–2x.
14. **SpeedTool**
    - The slider becomes logarithmic, with pure `speedToSlider`/`sliderToSpeed` in `model/` and presets 0.1/0.5/1/2/5/10/100.
    - A "Keep pitch" switch, and a "3.2s → 1.6s" length label.
    - Sped-up clips keep their 60 fps cap. I'll check on device how preview and export cope at 100x.

## D. Ratio
15. **`AspectRatio`**
    - Adds `ORIGINAL`, `RATIO_4_3`, `RATIO_3_4`, `RATIO_2_1`, `RATIO_235_100`, `RATIO_185_100` and `RATIO_9_19_5` (as 18:39).
    - New pure `Project.outputSize()` in `model/OutputSize.kt`. It resolves ORIGINAL from the first clip's displayed dimensions, after source rotation, and falls back to 9:16.
    - It replaces `outputSizeFor(project.aspectRatio)` in `CompositionSpec` and `TextPositionOverlay`.
    - `RatioTool` becomes a scrolling row.

## E. Text
16. **Rows:** a generic pure `stackIntoLanes(items, start, end, id)` in `model/Lanes.kt` (`audioLanes` is refactored onto it) plus `Project.textLanes()`. `TextLane` becomes `TextRows` (one row per lane), and `timelineHeight` counts the text rows.
17. **Transform on the preview**
    - New `TextOverlay.rotationDegrees: Float = 0f` (clockwise) and `opacity: Float = 1f`.
    - `TextPositionOverlay` becomes `TextTransformOverlay`:
      - Its gesture detector covers the whole preview area. One finger moves the text only if the gesture started on it; two fingers pinch (scaling `textSizeSp`, clamped 8–160) and rotate.
      - It snaps to the centre lines (guide lines drawn, haptic) and to 0/90/180/270° within 5°.
      - The result is committed on release as one `UpdateText`.
    - `TextSpec` gains `rotationDegrees`/`opacity`, and `TimedTextOverlay` applies `setRotationDegrees(-deg)` and `setAlphaScale(opacity)`.
18. **Colour:** a custom swatch in `TextTool` opens `ColorPickerSheet`, a new composable with:
    - a hue bar and a saturation/value square
    - a hex field
    - "recent" colours, which are the colours already used in this project's texts
    `TextTool` gets an opacity slider, and is split into `TextTool` plus `TextStyleRow` to stay under 150 lines.
19. **Split and duplicate:** new actions `SplitText(id, atMs, newId)` and `DuplicateText(id, newId)`. The duplicate starts at the original's end and stacks if it would overlap. Both are icons in the text panel header.

## F. Tests (JVM)
- `insertIndexAt`
- `Batch`: one history step, and skipping photos and audio
- `stackIntoLanes` for text
- `SplitText` and `DuplicateText`
- the speed range, `keepPitch`, and the speed slider log mapping
- `Project.outputSize()` for every ratio, including ORIGINAL with rotated sources
- `rulerTicks` in frame mode
- `snapEdge`
- text rotation and opacity in the spec mapping
- the cover key from a chosen frame or image
- the janitor sweeping all three directories
- `HomeViewModel` consuming a share
- A serializer round-trip of a Phase 6 JSON without the new fields, to prove drafts still load.

## Files (main)
- **model:**
  - changed: `Enums.kt`, `Clip.kt`, `TextOverlay.kt`, `Project.kt`, `OutputSize.kt`, `TimelineMath.kt`, `edit/EditAction.kt`, `edit/EditReducer.kt`
  - new: `Lanes.kt`, `ProjectCover.kt`, `SpeedScale.kt`
- **media:**
  - changed: `CompositionSpec.kt`, `CompositionBuilder.kt`, `EffectsFactory.kt`, `TimedTextOverlay.kt`, `ProjectCoverMaker.kt`, `MediaImporter.kt`
  - new: `CaptureFiles.kt`, `SharedMediaCopier.kt`, `CoverOverlay.kt`
- **data:** `VoiceoverJanitor.kt` renamed to `AppMediaJanitor.kt`; new `ShareInbox.kt`.
- **UI:**
  - changed: `MainActivity`, `AppNavHost`, `HomeScreen`/`HomeContent`/`HomeViewModel`, `EditorViewModel`, `EditorScreen`, `EditorBottomPanel`, `TimelineSection`, `timeline/*` (Ruler, ClipView, TimelineBar, TrimHandle, TimelineLanes, TextLane, Timeline), `tools/SpeedTool`, `RatioTool`, `TextTool`, `FilterTool`, `ClipVolumeTool`
  - new: `SelectionToolbar`, `CoverTool`, `ColorPickerSheet`, `FullScreenPreview`, `EdgeAutoScroller`, `ClipBadges`, `AddMediaMenu`
- **Also:**
  - `AndroidManifest.xml`: the provider, share intent filters and `singleTask`
  - `res/xml/file_paths.xml` and `strings.xml`
- If the ViewModel grows past ~500 lines, multi-select and cover logic move into `EditorSelection` and `EditorCover`, following the same pattern as `EditorAudio`/`EditorHost`.

## Verification
`./gradlew assembleDebug` and `testDebugUnitTest` after each block (A–E). Then on device:
1. **Share:** share 2 videos from Gallery to PreCut. A new project opens, and it still works after the gallery originals are deleted.
2. **Camera:** with the playhead in the middle of clip 2, record a video. It lands after clip 2. Take a photo; it inserts too.
3. **Full-screen:** play, scrub, rotate the device, and Back.
4. **Trimming:** trim a clip edge near the playhead; it snaps with a tick. Drag a text bar to the screen edge; the timeline auto-scrolls.
5. **Frame zoom:** zoom in fully. The ruler shows `5f`/`10f`, and the badges show speed and duration.
6. **Select:** select 2 clips and a text, then Delete. One Undo restores all three. Set speed on several clips at once, and use Apply-to-all for the filter.
7. **Cover:** set a cover frame. The drafts grid shows it, and with "first frame" on, the exported video's gallery thumbnail is the cover.
8. **Speed:** 0.1x and 100x on a clip, with pitch on and off. The preview and export should agree.

# Phase 7 — Core editing parity (CapCut audit of Phases 1–4)

## Context
Phase 6 is approved and committed (`ae57547`). The per-phase CapCut audit in `docs/PLAN.md` §6 found gaps in what Phases 1–4 built: import and preview, timeline, speed and ratio, and text. Phase 7 closes them before the bigger visual phases start. Everything runs on-device with Media3 1.11.1. I checked the one new Media3 API this phase uses: `StaticOverlaySettings.Builder.setRotationDegrees` exists (counter-clockwise, so it gets negated like clip rotation).

The work is in 6 blocks. I build and test after each one.

## A. Import and preview
1. **Insert at the playhead**
   - Pure `Project.insertIndexAt(timelineMs)` in `model/TimelineMath.kt`. It returns the clip boundary nearest the playhead: before the clip if the playhead is in its first half, after it otherwise, and the end of the list when empty or at the end.
   - `EditorViewModel.onMediaPicked` passes it as `AddClips.atIndex`.
2. **Camera**
   - The editor's `+` becomes a small menu: *Photos & videos* / *Record video* / *Take photo*. Home gets a camera action next to "New project".
   - Uses the `CaptureVideo` / `TakePicture` contracts with a `FileProvider` Uri into `filesDir/captures/<uuid>.mp4|jpg`. Intents don't need the CAMERA permission.
   - The stored clip Uri is `Uri.fromFile(...)`, which is our own file. New `media/CaptureFiles.kt` creates the file and both Uris.
   - Manifest gets a `<provider>`, plus `res/xml/file_paths.xml` covering only `captures/`.
3. **Share to PreCut**
   - `MainActivity` gets intent filters for `ACTION_SEND` / `ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE` with `video/*` and `image/*`, and `launchMode="singleTask"`; `onNewIntent` handles shares too.
   - Shared Uris only have temporary read grants, so new `media/SharedMediaCopier` copies them into `filesDir/imports/` with a progress state. A singleton `ShareInbox` (StateFlow) hands them over.
   - `AppNavHost` pops back to Home, and `HomeViewModel` consumes the inbox: copy, then the existing import path, then a new project, then OpenEditor.
   - `AndroidMediaImporter` skips `takePersistableUriPermission` for `file://` Uris.
4. **Cleanup:** the Phase 6 `VoiceoverJanitor` becomes `AppMediaJanitor`. It sweeps `voiceovers/`, `captures/` and `imports/` for files no project references (same rule: only on the Projects screen).
5. **Full-screen preview**
   - A `fullScreen` flag in `Ready` and a button on `PlaybackControls`.
   - `FullScreenPreview` uses the same player and overlays the whole screen, with a scrub `Slider`, play/pause, time and close. It hides the system bars with `WindowInsetsControllerCompat`, and `BackHandler` closes it.

## B. Timeline
6. **Trim snapping:** `ClipView` handles snap the dragged edge to the playhead and to text/audio edges and beats. They reuse `snapTargetsOf` and `TimelineGeometry.snapMove`'s threshold, with a haptic tick. A new pure `TimelineGeometry.snapEdge(edgeMs, targets, threshold)` does the work. While dragging, the start handle visually follows the finger (the clip's content is offset by the drag), as in CapCut.
7. **Auto-scroll near edges**
   - New `EdgeAutoScroller` (provided by `Timeline` through a CompositionLocal, holding the `ScrollState` and viewport width). While a bar or trim handle drag is within 48dp of the viewport edge, it scrolls with speed proportional to depth. It reports the scrolled px back to the drag so the edge stays under the finger.
   - It's used by `TimelineBar`, `TrimHandle` and `ClipView`.
8. **Frame-level zoom and ruler**
   - `MAX_DP_PER_SECOND` goes from 480 to 1500, about 50dp per frame at 30 fps.
   - New pure `TimelineGeometry.rulerTicks(pxPerMs, minSpacingPx, totalMs)`. Below 100 ms it switches to frame ticks (30 fps, as CapCut uses) labelled `5f`, `10f`…, and seconds stay labelled. `TimelineRuler` draws its output.
9. **Clip badges:**
   - a speed badge (`2.0x`) on any clip whose speed isn't 1
   - the duration (`3.2s`) at the top-left of the selected clip
   - the existing muted badge
   All three go in a small `ClipBadges` composable, so `ClipView` stays under 150 lines.
10. **Multi-select**
    - The main toolbar gets **Select**, which sets `Ready.multiSelect: Set<String>?`; non-null means select mode.
    - In select mode, taps toggle clips, texts and audio clips through the existing `onSelectClip`/`onTextSelected`/`audio.onSelected` routes, checked in the ViewModel. They draw a selected border without handles.
    - The bottom bar becomes `SelectionToolbar`: a count, then *Delete, Duplicate, Speed, Filter, Volume, Done*. Speed, Filter and Volume reuse `SpeedTool`, `FilterTool` and `VolumeSlider`.
    - Undo: a new `EditAction.Batch(actions: List<EditAction>)` folds through the reducer, so a batch is one history step. Speed and Filter skip photos and audio; Volume covers clips and audio.
11. **Apply to all:** a button in `FilterTool` and `ClipVolumeTool` that sends a `Batch` covering every clip.
12. **Project cover**
    - `Project.cover: ProjectCover?`: either `Frame(timelineMs)` or `Image(uri)`. It's chosen with a new **Cover** tool (main toolbar), which offers a frame scrubber over the preview or *From gallery*.
    - `ProjectCoverMaker.keyFor`/`make` use the chosen cover: they find the frame through `clipAt` plus `ThumbnailLoader`, or decode the image.
    - `Project.coverInExport` (a switch in the panel): the composition-level overlay shows the cover full-frame for the first frame only, through a new `CoverOverlay` (a `BitmapOverlay` loaded lazily on the effects thread). Timing stays identical in preview and export.

## C. Speed (clip)
13. **Range and pitch**
    - The range becomes 0.1x–100x: `MIN_SPEED`/`MAX_SPEED` in `EditReducer`.
    - New `Clip.keepPitch = true`, set by a new `SetKeepPitch` action and mapped to `SpeedParameters(..., shouldMaintainPitch)`. Audio-clip speed stays 0.5–2x.
14. **SpeedTool**
    - The slider becomes logarithmic, with pure `speedToSlider`/`sliderToSpeed` in `model/` and presets 0.1/0.5/1/2/5/10/100.
    - A "Keep pitch" switch, and a "3.2s → 1.6s" length label.
    - Sped-up clips keep their 60 fps cap. I'll check on device how preview and export cope at 100x.

## D. Ratio
15. **`AspectRatio`**
    - Adds `ORIGINAL`, `RATIO_4_3`, `RATIO_3_4`, `RATIO_2_1`, `RATIO_235_100`, `RATIO_185_100` and `RATIO_9_19_5` (as 18:39).
    - New pure `Project.outputSize()` in `model/OutputSize.kt`. It resolves ORIGINAL from the first clip's displayed dimensions, after source rotation, and falls back to 9:16.
    - It replaces `outputSizeFor(project.aspectRatio)` in `CompositionSpec` and `TextPositionOverlay`.
    - `RatioTool` becomes a scrolling row.

## E. Text
16. **Rows:** a generic pure `stackIntoLanes(items, start, end, id)` in `model/Lanes.kt` (`audioLanes` is refactored onto it) plus `Project.textLanes()`. `TextLane` becomes `TextRows` (one row per lane), and `timelineHeight` counts the text rows.
17. **Transform on the preview**
    - New `TextOverlay.rotationDegrees: Float = 0f` (clockwise) and `opacity: Float = 1f`.
    - `TextPositionOverlay` becomes `TextTransformOverlay`:
      - Its gesture detector covers the whole preview area. One finger moves the text only if the gesture started on it; two fingers pinch (scaling `textSizeSp`, clamped 8–160) and rotate.
      - It snaps to the centre lines (guide lines drawn, haptic) and to 0/90/180/270° within 5°.
      - The result is committed on release as one `UpdateText`.
    - `TextSpec` gains `rotationDegrees`/`opacity`, and `TimedTextOverlay` applies `setRotationDegrees(-deg)` and `setAlphaScale(opacity)`.
18. **Colour:** a custom swatch in `TextTool` opens `ColorPickerSheet`, a new composable with:
    - a hue bar and a saturation/value square
    - a hex field
    - "recent" colours, which are the colours already used in this project's texts
    `TextTool` gets an opacity slider, and is split into `TextTool` plus `TextStyleRow` to stay under 150 lines.
19. **Split and duplicate:** new actions `SplitText(id, atMs, newId)` and `DuplicateText(id, newId)`. The duplicate starts at the original's end and stacks if it would overlap. Both are icons in the text panel header.

  - new: `Lanes.kt`, `ProjectCover.kt`, `SpeedScale.kt`

Phase 7 closes them before the bigger visual phases start. Everything runs on-device with Media3 1.11.1. I checked the one new Media3 API this phase uses: `StaticOverlaySettings.Builder.setRotationDegrees` exists (counter-clockwise, so it gets negated like clip rotation).

-The current uncommitted Phase 5 work is the starting point. These pieces are reused or generalized: `TimelineBar`, `VolumeSlider`, the `GainProcessor` path in `EffectsFactory`, the `OpenDocument` picker, `importAudio`, `placementWithin` (generalized to speed), `ClipVolumeTool` and the muted badge.
+The work is in 6 blocks. I build and test after each one.
-## Feature set (CapCut parity, minus AI and online libraries)

-- **Multi-track audio:** any number of audio clips. Overlapping clips automatically stack onto extra rows (CapCut behaviour). Clip types are **Music** (device file), **Voiceover** (recorded) and **Extracted** (from a video clip), each with its own colour.

-- **Per audio clip:** move, trim, split at the playhead, duplicate, delete, replace, volume 0–200%, fade in/out, speed 0.5–2× (pitch kept), voice effects (pitch presets: Chipmunk, High, Deep, Monster), and beats.
-- **Waveforms** drawn on every audio clip, decoded on-device and cached.
-- **Voiceover:** record from the mic starting at the playhead. While recording, a timer shows and the preview plays muted (avoids echo). Stopping drops the recording on the timeline.
-- **Extract audio** from a video clip: its sound becomes an Extracted audio clip at the same time (same trim and speed), and the video clip is muted.
-- **"Mute clip audio" toggle** at the left of the clip strip mutes all original video sound at once (project-level, like CapCut).

# Phase 5 rebuild: CapCut-style audio

## Context
Phase 5 (one background-music track, clip volume and mute) is built but not committed. The user wants audio rebuilt to match CapCut, with **every audio feature except AI-based ones** (no noise reduction or AI voice/vocal isolation). Music comes from **device files only**, since a Sounds library needs licensed content and a server. Everything below runs on-device with Media3 1.11.1:
- fades: `DefaultGainProvider.addFadeAt`
- voice pitch: `SonicAudioProcessor.setPitch`
- speed on secondary sequences: `SpeedChangingMediaSource` in CompositionPlayer, `ExoPlayerAssetLoader` in Transformer
- multiple audio-only `EditedMediaItemSequence`s with gaps

The current uncommitted Phase 5 work is the starting point. These pieces are reused or generalized: `TimelineBar`, `VolumeSlider`, the `GainProcessor` path in `EffectsFactory`, the `OpenDocument` picker, `importAudio`, `placementWithin` (generalized to speed), `ClipVolumeTool` and the muted badge.

## Feature set (CapCut parity, minus AI and online libraries)
- **Multi-track audio:** any number of audio clips. Overlapping clips automatically stack onto extra rows (CapCut behaviour). Clip types are **Music** (device file), **Voiceover** (recorded) and **Extracted** (from a video clip), each with its own colour.
- **Per audio clip:** move, trim, split at the playhead, duplicate, delete, replace, volume 0–200%, fade in/out, speed 0.5–2× (pitch kept), voice effects (pitch presets: Chipmunk, High, Deep, Monster), and beats.
- **Waveforms** drawn on every audio clip, decoded on-device and cached.
- **Voiceover:** record from the mic starting at the playhead. While recording, a timer shows and the preview plays muted (avoids echo). Stopping drops the recording on the timeline.
- **Extract audio** from a video clip: its sound becomes an Extracted audio clip at the same time (same trim and speed), and the video clip is muted.
- **"Mute clip audio" toggle** at the left of the clip strip mutes all original video sound at once (project-level, like CapCut).
- **Video clips' own sound:** volume, mute (already done), fade in/out, extract audio.
- **Beats:** tap to add or remove beat markers at the playhead on an audio clip, or clear them. Markers show as dots. While dragging, text and audio bars **snap** to beats and to the playhead (within about 10dp, with a haptic tick).
- **Out of scope:** noise reduction, AI voice changers and vocal isolation, auto-beat detection, and online sound libraries.

## Model (`model/`, pure; replaces the single-track actions)
- `AudioClip` gets new fields: `kind` (MUSIC, VOICEOVER, EXTRACTED), `speed`, `fadeInMs`, `fadeOutMs`, `voiceEffect` (NONE, CHIPMUNK, HIGH, DEEP, MONSTER, each with a pitch factor) and `beatsMs` (source time).

- `Project` gets `originalAudioMuted`.
- **`AudioLanes.kt`:**
  - `audioLanes(project): List<List<AudioClip>>`: greedy interval stacking, sorted by start then id so it's deterministic.
  - `timelineDurationMs()` for audio (speed-aware), and `placementWithin` generalized to speed.
- **`EditAction` / `EditReducer`:**
  - Audio clips: `AddAudio`, `DeleteAudio`, `SplitAudio(id, atTimelineMs, newId)`, `DuplicateAudio(id, newId)` (placed right after the original), `ReplaceAudio`, `SetAudioTiming`, `SetAudioVolume`, `SetAudioFades`, `SetAudioSpeed`, `SetVoiceEffect`, `ToggleBeat(id, atTimelineMs)`, `ClearBeats`.
  - Video clips and project: `SetClipFades`, `SetOriginalAudioMuted`, `ExtractAudio(clipId, newAudioId)`.
  - Fades are clamped so in + out ≤ the clip's length. Splitting divides beats between the halves, and the fade-out stays on the second half only.
- The Phase 5 single-track actions (`SetMusic`, `RemoveMusic`, `SetMusicTiming`, `SetMusicVolume`) are removed.

## Media
- **`CompositionSpec`:**
  - Video items get `fadeInMs` and `fadeOutMs`. Volume is 0 when the clip is muted or `originalAudioMuted` is on.
  - `audioLanes: List<List<AudioItemSpec>>`. Each item has `gapBeforeMs`, the clip range already cut at the video end, speed, volume, fades and pitch.
- **`CompositionBuilder`:** builds one audio-only sequence per lane, using `addGap` before each item.

  - then `SonicAudioProcessor` with the pitch

- Lane stacking: overlaps, touching edges, stable ordering, and stacking after a move.
- Reducer: every new action, including split dividing beats and fades, extract (timing matches the clip and the clip gets muted), fade clamping, and speed and duration changes.

- `snapMs`, music drag (existing), and waveform peak bucketing (a pure function over a PCM array).

1. Add 2 songs overlapping in time; they should stack on 2 rows with waveforms, and both play mixed.
2. Split a song, move the second half, fade it in and out, set it to 50% and 1.5×. Preview and export should match.
3. Record a voiceover at 0:03. It should appear at 0:03 and play back. Apply Deep; it should sound lower and keep its length.

package com.savie.precut.model

import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
import kotlin.math.roundToLong

/** Where an audio clip came from; also picks its colour on the timeline. */
@Serializable
enum class AudioKind { MUSIC, VOICEOVER, EXTRACTED }

/** Pitch-shift presets (duration unchanged). */
@Serializable
enum class VoiceEffect(val pitch: Float) {
    NONE(1f),
    CHIPMUNK(1.8f),
    HIGH(1.3f),
    DEEP(0.78f),
    MONSTER(0.6f),
}

/**
 * An audio clip on an audio lane: plays source range [trimStartMs, trimEndMs) at [speed], starting
 * at [timelineStartMs]. Fades are in timeline time; beats are in source time.
 */
@Serializable
data class AudioClip(
    val id: String,
    val uri: String,
    val sourceDurationMs: Long,
    val timelineStartMs: Long = 0,
    val trimStartMs: Long = 0,
    val trimEndMs: Long,
    val volume: Float = 1f,
    /** File name shown on the lane. */
    val displayName: String = "",
    val kind: AudioKind = AudioKind.MUSIC,
    val speed: Float = 1f,
    val fadeInMs: Long = 0,
    val fadeOutMs: Long = 0,
    val voiceEffect: VoiceEffect = VoiceEffect.NONE,
    val beatsMs: List<Long> = emptyList(),
)

/** Length on the timeline: `(trimEnd - trimStart) / speed`. */
fun AudioClip.timelineDurationMs(): Long = ((trimEndMs - trimStartMs) / speed.toDouble()).roundToLong()

fun AudioClip.timelineEndMs(): Long = timelineStartMs + timelineDurationMs()

/** Source time under timeline time [timelineMs] (not clamped). */
fun AudioClip.sourceAt(timelineMs: Long): Long = trimStartMs + ((timelineMs - timelineStartMs) * speed.toDouble()).roundToLong()

/** Timeline time of source time [sourceMs] (not clamped). */
fun AudioClip.timelineAt(sourceMs: Long): Long = timelineStartMs + ((sourceMs - trimStartMs) / speed.toDouble()).roundToLong()

/** The part of an audio clip that actually plays: it is cut at the video's end. */
data class AudioPlacement(
    val timelineStartMs: Long,
    val timelineDurationMs: Long,
    val sourceStartMs: Long,
    val sourceEndMs: Long,
)

/**
 * Where the clip plays inside a video of [videoDurationMs]. Audio running past the video end is
 * cut there; audio starting at or after the end doesn't play (null).
 */
fun AudioClip.placementWithin(videoDurationMs: Long): AudioPlacement? {
    val available = videoDurationMs - timelineStartMs
    if (available <= 0L) return null
    val length = minOf(timelineDurationMs(), available)
    if (length <= 0L) return null
    val sourceEnd = if (length == timelineDurationMs()) trimEndMs else sourceAt(timelineStartMs + length).coerceAtMost(trimEndMs)
    return AudioPlacement(timelineStartMs, length, trimStartMs, sourceEnd)
}

    data class SetClipVolume(val clipId: String, val volume: Float) : EditAction

    data class SetClipMuted(val clipId: String, val muted: Boolean) : EditAction
