tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

package com.savie.precut.ui.home

import androidx.compose.animation.AnimatedVisibility
import androidx.compose.animation.scaleIn

import androidx.compose.material3.SnackbarHost

import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.derivedStateOf

import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.res.painterResource
import androidx.compose.ui.res.stringResource
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.savie.precut.R
import com.savie.precut.data.ProjectSummary
import com.savie.precut.ui.theme.AccentFill
import com.savie.precut.ui.theme.OnAccent
import com.savie.precut.ui.theme.PreCutType
import com.savie.precut.ui.theme.TextSecondary

/** What the drafts grid can do with a project. */
interface ProjectActions {
    fun onOpen(projectId: String)
    fun onRename(projectId: String, name: String)
    fun onDuplicate(projectId: String)
    fun onDelete(projectId: String)
}

/** Projects screen: drafts grid (H-02), empty state (H-01) or importing (H-07). */
@Composable
fun HomeContent(
    isImporting: Boolean,
    projects: List<ProjectSummary>?,
    snackbarHostState: SnackbarHostState,
    onNewProject: () -> Unit,
    onCamera: (video: Boolean) -> Unit,
    actions: ProjectActions,
) {
    var renaming by remember { mutableStateOf<ProjectSummary?>(null) }
    var deleting by remember { mutableStateOf<ProjectSummary?>(null) }
    val gridState = rememberLazyStaggeredGridState()
    // Hidden while scrolling down the drafts, back as soon as the user scrolls up.
    val fabVisible by remember { derivedStateOf { !gridState.canScrollBackward || !gridState.lastScrolledForward } }

    Scaffold(
        topBar = { HomeTopBar(cameraEnabled = !isImporting, onCamera = onCamera) },
        snackbarHost = { SnackbarHost(snackbarHostState) },
        floatingActionButton = {
            AnimatedVisibility(!isImporting && !projects.isNullOrEmpty() && fabVisible, enter = scaleIn(), exit = scaleOut()) {
                FloatingActionButton(
                    onClick = onNewProject,
                    shape = RoundedCornerShape(16.dp),
                    containerColor = AccentFill,
                    contentColor = OnAccent,
                    modifier = Modifier.size(56.dp),
                ) {
                    Icon(painterResource(R.drawable.ic_add), contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.home_new_project))
                }
            }
        },
    ) { innerPadding ->
        val modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(innerPadding)
        when {
            isImporting -> ImportingMedia(modifier)
            projects == null -> Box(modifier, contentAlignment = Alignment.Center) { CircularProgressIndicator() }
            projects.isEmpty() -> EmptyProjects(onNewProject, modifier)
            else -> LazyVerticalStaggeredGrid(
                columns = StaggeredGridCells.Fixed(2),
                state = gridState,
                contentPadding = PaddingValues(start = 16.dp, end = 16.dp, top = 4.dp, bottom = 120.dp),
                horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp),
                verticalItemSpacing = 16.dp,
                modifier = modifier,
            ) {
                item(span = StaggeredGridItemSpan.FullLine) {
                    Text(stringResource(R.string.home_drafts_count, projects.size), style = PreCutType.section, color = TextSecondary)
                }
                items(projects, key = { it.id }) { project ->
                    ProjectCard(
                        project = project,
                        onOpen = { actions.onOpen(project.id) },
                        onRename = { renaming = project },
                        onDuplicate = { actions.onDuplicate(project.id) },
                        onDelete = { deleting = project },
                    )
                }
            }
        }
    }

    renaming?.let { project ->
        RenameDialog(
            initialName = displayName(project),
            onConfirm = { name ->
                actions.onRename(project.id, name)
                renaming = null
            },
            onDismiss = { renaming = null },
        )
    }
    deleting?.let { project ->
        DeleteDialog(
            name = displayName(project),
            onConfirm = {
                actions.onDelete(project.id)
                deleting = null
            },
            onDismiss = { deleting = null },
        )
    }
}

/** What the drafts grid can do with a project. */
interface ProjectActions {
    fun onOpen(projectId: String)
    fun onRename(projectId: String, name: String)
    fun onDuplicate(projectId: String)
    fun onDelete(projectId: String)
}

/** Projects screen: drafts grid (H-02), empty state (H-01) or importing (H-07). */
@Composable
fun HomeContent(
    isImporting: Boolean,
    projects: List<ProjectSummary>?,
    snackbarHostState: SnackbarHostState,
    onNewProject: () -> Unit,
    onCamera: (video: Boolean) -> Unit,
    actions: ProjectActions,
) {
    var renaming by remember { mutableStateOf<ProjectSummary?>(null) }
    var deleting by remember { mutableStateOf<ProjectSummary?>(null) }
    val gridState = rememberLazyStaggeredGridState()
    // Hidden while scrolling down the drafts, back as soon as the user scrolls up.
    val fabVisible by remember { derivedStateOf { !gridState.canScrollBackward || !gridState.lastScrolledForward } }

    Scaffold(
        topBar = { HomeTopBar(cameraEnabled = !isImporting, onCamera = onCamera) },
        snackbarHost = { SnackbarHost(snackbarHostState) },
        floatingActionButton = {
            AnimatedVisibility(!isImporting && !projects.isNullOrEmpty() && fabVisible, enter = scaleIn(), exit = scaleOut()) {
                FloatingActionButton(
                    onClick = onNewProject,
                    shape = RoundedCornerShape(16.dp),
                    containerColor = AccentFill,
                    contentColor = OnAccent,
                    modifier = Modifier.size(56.dp),
                ) {
                    Icon(painterResource(R.drawable.ic_add), contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.home_new_project))
                }
            }
        },
    ) { innerPadding ->
        val modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(innerPadding)
        when {
            isImporting -> ImportingMedia(modifier)
            projects == null -> Box(modifier, contentAlignment = Alignment.Center) { CircularProgressIndicator() }
            projects.isEmpty() -> EmptyProjects(onNewProject, modifier)
            else -> LazyVerticalStaggeredGrid(
                columns = StaggeredGridCells.Fixed(2),
                state = gridState,
                contentPadding = PaddingValues(start = 16.dp, end = 16.dp, top = 4.dp, bottom = 120.dp),
                horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp),
                verticalItemSpacing = 16.dp,
                modifier = modifier,
            ) {
                item(span = StaggeredGridItemSpan.FullLine) {
                    Text(stringResource(R.string.home_drafts_count, projects.size), style = PreCutType.section, color = TextSecondary)
                }
                items(projects, key = { it.id }) { project ->
                    ProjectCard(
                        project = project,
                        onOpen = { actions.onOpen(project.id) },
                        onRename = { renaming = project },
                        onDuplicate = { actions.onDuplicate(project.id) },
                        onDelete = { deleting = project },
                    )
                }
            }
        }
    }

    renaming?.let { project ->
        RenameDialog(
            initialName = displayName(project),
            onConfirm = { name ->
                actions.onRename(project.id, name)
                renaming = null
            },
            onDismiss = { renaming = null },
        )
    }
    deleting?.let { project ->
        DeleteDialog(
            name = displayName(project),
            onConfirm = {
                actions.onDelete(project.id)
                deleting = null
            },
            onDismiss = { deleting = null },
        )
    }
}

**8B — Frame**
- [ ] **Transform main clips:** drag, pinch-scale and rotate any angle on the preview; Fit / Fill; snap to centre and 0°/90°
- [ ] **Crop:** free and fixed ratios on the preview; **Mirror** horizontal / vertical
- [ ] **Canvas / background:** black, colour, blur (4 strengths), or an image; apply to all
- [ ] **Opacity** per clip

**8C — Motion and time**
- [ ] **Edge transitions** between clips (no overlap, total length unchanged): fade through black/white, flash, zoom in/out, blur, glitch, spin; adjustable duration; apply to all. Overlapping transitions come in Phase 9
- [ ] **Clip animations** in/out/combo with duration: fade, zoom, slide, spin, bounce, shake
- [ ] **Speed curves:** presets (Montage, Hero, Bullet, Jump cut, Flash in/out) and a custom curve editor with draggable points; variable `SpeedProvider`; timeline math handles variable speed
- [ ] **Freeze frame:** insert a still (photo clip) of the frame under the playhead, splitting the clip
- [ ] **Reverse:** pre-render a reversed copy with a progress dialog, cached in app storage; undo restores the original (prototype first; stretch if unreliable across devices)
- [ ] **Motion blur** (CapCut Pro): frame blending with `FrameCache` — stretch goal
- [x] **Replace clip** (keeps position, length and settings) — built in Phase 6 for missing media
- [ ] Unit tests for every new action and spec mapping (curve integration, transition edge timing)

**Acceptance:** a project with a LUT filter at 60%, HSL + curves, a filter layer, a transformed and cropped clip, blurred canvas, 2 transitions, an animation, a speed curve, a freeze frame and a reversed clip exports identically to the preview.

### Phase 8.5 — Design refresh (Claude Design screens)
Apply the Claude Design system (`docs/design/DESIGN.md`, `docs/design/claude-design/`) to everything already built. Two stops, each with a device check:

**8.5a — Theme, components, editor**

- [ ] Unit tests: keyframe interpolation and easing, overlay placement/lanes, compositor settings mapping, A/B transition layout

- [ ] Stroke (outline), shadow (colour, blur, distance, angle), glow, text box background with corner radius and padding

- [ ] Text animations in/out/loop with duration (fade, typewriter, slide, pop, bounce, wave)

- [ ] Stickers: emoji picker and device images (PNG/WebP, animated GIF/WebP via `ImageDecoder` frames) on a sticker lane; transform on preview; animations; keyframes (reuse Phase 9)

content.text:
Phase 8.5b is finished, and with it the whole design refresh. Everything compiles with no warnings, and the unit tests pass. I ticked 8.5b in [PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) and added a decisions-log entry. One box is still open, the 412 dp and 360 dp width check, because it needs your device.

**What changed in this phase**
- **Panels:** Trim, Speed, Volume, Fade, Filters, Adjust, HSL, Curves, Ratio, Cover, Text, the colour picker, the audio panels and Voiceover all follow their frames. Filters has a new before/after peek: tap the filter that's already selected to see the frame without it.
- **Projects screen:**
  - New top bar with the logo.
  - Drafts are in a two-column grid where each cover keeps its own shape, with "Drafts · N" above it.
  - Each card shows a duration badge, the name and "Edited …", and has a ⋮ menu. Long-press opens the same menu, and Delete is in red.
  - The add button hides as you scroll down and comes back when you scroll up.
  - There's a new empty screen ("Start your first video"), a new importing screen, and restyled dialogs.
  - Files: [HomeContent.kt](app/src/main/java/com/savie/precut/ui/home/HomeContent.kt), [HomeTopBar.kt](app/src/main/java/com/savie/precut/ui/home/HomeTopBar.kt), [HomeStates.kt](app/src/main/java/com/savie/precut/ui/home/HomeStates.kt), [ProjectCard.kt](app/src/main/java/com/savie/precut/ui/home/ProjectCard.kt), [ProjectDialogs.kt](app/src/main/java/com/savie/precut/ui/home/ProjectDialogs.kt)
- **Export:** the progress screen shows a ring around the cover; the done screen has Open and Share buttons and a way back to Projects.
- **App icon and splash:** the new logo, including the monochrome themed icon and the Android 12 splash.
- I removed the old Material icons library, since every icon now comes from the new set.

**Where it differs from the design** (all logged in PLAN.md)
- **Speed "Curve" tab:** it shows "Soon"; speed curves come in Phase 8C.
- **Settings button:** it's left off the Projects bar until Phase 12.
- **Importing screen:** it has no "2 of 3 · 64%" count and no Cancel button, because the importer can't report progress or be cancelled yet. It shows a moving bar instead.

**Device test steps**
1. **Projects, empty:** delete every draft. You should see the empty screen with a full-width New project button, and tapping it opens the picker.
2. **Projects, grid:**
   - Make drafts with portrait (9:16) and square (1:1) covers; the two columns should show different heights.
   - Check that each card has a duration badge and an "Edited …" line.
   - Scroll down and the add button hides; scroll up and it comes back.
3. **Menu and dialogs:**
   - Tap ⋮ and long-press a card; both open the same menu.
   - Rename updates the card, Duplicate adds a copy, and Delete (red) asks before removing.
4. **Importing:** pick several videos. You should see "Preparing your media…" with a moving bar, then the editor opens. Try sharing into the app from the gallery too.
5. **Panels:** open each tool and compare it with its frame. In Filters, tap the selected filter again and the frame should show without the filter until you close the panel. Speed should snap to 1x.
6. **Text:** the text box has a dashed outline; ✕ deletes the text, and the corner handle rotates and resizes it.
7. **Export:** check the ring progress, then on the done screen try Open, Share and the home button.
8. **Icon and splash:** look at the launcher icon with themed icons on and off, and check the splash on a cold start.
9. **Narrow screens:** repeat the Projects and editor checks at 360 dp width (set Display size to largest).

Suggested commit:

```
style: design refresh — panels, projects, export, app icon (Phase 8.5b)
```

package com.savie.precut.ui.editor.tools

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.foundation.background
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.size

import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalResources
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.savie.precut.R

/** What the multi-select toolbar can do with the picked items. */
interface SelectionActions {
    fun onDone()
    fun onDelete()
    fun onDuplicate()
    fun onSpeed()
    fun onFilter()
    fun onVolume()
}

/** Toolbar in multi-select mode: the count, then edits applied to every picked item at once. */
@Composable
fun SelectionToolbar(count: Int, hasClips: Boolean, actions: SelectionActions, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    val any = count > 0
    ToolRow(modifier) {
        ToolButton(R.drawable.ic_check, R.string.action_done, onClick = actions::onDone)
        Text(
            LocalResources.current.getQuantityString(R.plurals.selection_count, count, count),
            style = PreCutType.labelChip.copy(fontWeight = FontWeight.SemiBold),
            maxLines = 1,
            modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterVertically).padding(horizontal = 8.dp),
        )
        Box(Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterVertically).padding(horizontal = 4.dp).size(width = 1.dp, height = 32.dp).background(Ink3))
        ToolButton(R.drawable.ic_delete, R.string.tool_delete, any, actions::onDelete)
        ToolButton(R.drawable.ic_duplicate, R.string.tool_duplicate, any, actions::onDuplicate)
        ToolButton(R.drawable.ic_speed, R.string.tool_speed, hasClips, actions::onSpeed)
        ToolButton(R.drawable.ic_filter, R.string.tool_filters, hasClips, actions::onFilter)
        ToolButton(R.drawable.ic_volume, R.string.tool_volume, any, actions::onVolume)
    }
}

content.text:
I've checked the design frames (T-12 to T-15, and the clip toolbar in E-04b) and the Media3 1.11.1 sources. Here is the Phase 8B plan for your approval. Nothing is coded yet.

## Phase 8B — Frame: plan

### Two places where Media3 doesn't do what we need
1. **Blurred background behind a moved clip.** Media3 has `GaussianBlurWithFrameOverlaid`, but it can only shrink the sharp frame evenly in the centre. It can't move or rotate it, and it can't show a frame that only fills part of the canvas. So I'll write our own shader effect, `CanvasEffect`, in the same way as 8A's `LookShaderProgram`.
   - It places the clip using Fit or Fill plus your transform, applies opacity, and draws it over the background (a colour, a blur of the clip filling the frame, or an image).
   - The blur runs on a frame shrunk to 1/8 size, so it stays cheap in both preview and export.
   - I checked the sources: Media3 leaves transparent pixels outside a moved frame, so this layering works.
   - Clips with default settings keep today's `Presentation` path, so nothing changes for existing projects.
2. **The preview can't follow your fingers live.** `CompositionPlayer` (Media3's preview player for edited projects) can't change an effect while it's playing, and rebuilding the preview for every finger movement would be far too slow. My proposal:
   - The effect reads a temporary value, used only by the preview, while a gesture or the opacity slider is moving.
   - The paused frame is redrawn by seeking to the same position in scrubbing mode.
   - On release, the change is saved and the preview is rebuilt through `CompositionBuilder`, so the saved result goes down exactly the same path as export.
   - **This needs your OK**, because it's a small preview-only hook, though not a second way of building the preview.
   - I'll test it first. If the redraw is too slow on your device, the fallback is that the outline follows your finger live and the video updates when you let go.

### Model (`model/`, pure Kotlin; old drafts load unchanged)
- New `Clip` fields:
  - `mirrored`
  - `crop: CropRect?` (0..1 rectangle) and `cropRatio`
  - `fit` (FIT or FILL)
  - `transform` (scale, any angle, x/y offset as a fraction of the frame)
  - `opacity`
  - `canvas: ClipCanvas` (Colour, Blur 1–4, or Image)
- I'm keeping a single Mirror control, matching the design. A vertical flip is Mirror plus a 180° rotation.
- Order of operations: mirror → 90° rotation → crop → Fit/Fill into the frame → your transform → opacity → canvas.
- When you rotate or mirror, the crop rectangle turns or flips with the picture, so it stays on what you chose.
- `FrameGeometry.kt` holds the clip's placement matrix, the crop maths and the snapping. Both the shader and the on-screen outline use it, so they always agree.
- New reducer actions:
  - SetCrop (one undo step from crop mode)
  - ToggleMirror
  - RotateClip (now also turns the crop)
  - SetTransform and SetFit
  - ResetTransform
  - SetOpacity
  - SetCanvas and ApplyCanvasToAll

### Media (`media/`)
- `CompositionSpec`: `VisualSpec` gains mirror, crop and a `FrameSpec`.
- `EffectsFactory` chain: Look → flip/rotate (`ScaleAndRotateTransformation`) → `Crop` → `CanvasEffect`, or `Presentation` for default clips.
- `CanvasShaderProgram`:
  - the background blur (shrink, then blur across, then down)
  - the clip placed on top with its opacity
  - the image background uploaded once
- `CanvasImages`:

- **Edit panel (T-12):** Crop, Mirror, Rotate.
- **Crop mode (T-12b):**
  - It takes over the screen with ✕ Crop ✓ at the top.
  - It works on a still of the frame at the playhead, with a thirds grid, corner and edge handles, and dragging inside to move.
  - The Ratio chips are Free, Original, 9:16, 16:9, 1:1 and 4:5, with Mirror and Rotate below.
  - ✓ saves it as one undo step; ✕ throws it away.
- **Transform (T-15):**
  - With a clip selected, touching the preview opens the Transform panel.
  - You can drag, pinch and twist, and it snaps to the centre lines and to 0°, 90°, 180° and 270° with a haptic tick.

  - The panel has Fit and Fill chips, Reset, and a "Scale 70% · 15° · X 0 · Y 0" readout.
  - It reuses the snapping code from text.
- **Canvas (T-13, T-13b, T-13c):**
  - Tabs for Colour, Blur and Image.
  - Colour has swatches plus the existing colour picker.
  - Blur has tiles for None, Light, Medium, Strong and Max.
  - Image has "From gallery" plus the four patterns.
  - There's an "Apply to all" button.
- **Opacity (T-14):** a slider showing the percentage, with Reset.

- placement maths: Fit/Fill at every ratio, plus scale, rotation and offset
- crop: conversion to Media3's coordinates, ratio locking, and what happens on rotate and mirror
- snapping
- every new reducer action and Apply to all
- the spec mapping, including that a default clip still uses the fast path
- loading an old draft's JSON

- Crop, mirror, rotate, transform, blurred canvas and opacity on a clip all look the same in preview and export.
- Old projects open and export exactly as before.

"""Converts Material Symbols Rounded SVGs into Android vector drawables: icons.py SYM RES name=symbol[:1] ..."""
import os, re, sys
sym, res, specs = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3:]
for spec in specs:
    res_name, symbol = spec.split('=')
    name, _, fill = symbol.partition(':')
    svg = open(os.path.join(sym, f"{name}{'_fill1' if fill else ''}_24px.svg")).read()
    paths = re.findall(r'<path d="([^"]+)"', svg)
    assert paths and 'viewBox="0 -960 960 960"' in svg, spec
    body = ''.join(f'''        <path
            android:fillColor="#FF000000"
            android:pathData="{d}" />
''' for d in paths)
    open(os.path.join(res, res_name + '.xml'), 'w').write(f'''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- Material Symbols Rounded "{name}"{" (filled)" if fill else ""}, weight 400 (Apache 2.0). -->
<vector xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:width="24dp"
    android:height="24dp"
    android:viewportWidth="960"
    android:viewportHeight="960">
    <group android:translateY="960">
{body}    </group>
</vector>
''')
print(len(specs), 'icons')

/**
 * Shell shared by every tool panel (replaces the toolbar while open): Ink1 with 16 dp top corners,
 * a 52 dp header (title, optional [actions], Done pill), then the body with 10 dp between rows.
 */
@Composable
fun ToolPanel(
    title: String,
    onDone: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    /** Extra header buttons, before Done (e.g. "Apply to all"). */
    actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit = {},
    /** A back arrow before the title (HSL and Curves return to Adjust). */
    onBack: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit,
) {
    Column(
        modifier
            .fillMaxWidth()
            .clip(RoundedCornerShape(topStart = 16.dp, topEnd = 16.dp))
            .background(Ink1),
    ) {
        Row(
            Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(52.dp).padding(start = if (onBack != null) 4.dp else 16.dp, end = 8.dp),
            verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
            horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(2.dp),
        ) {
            onBack?.let { back ->
                IconButton(onClick = back) {
                    Icon(painterResource(R.drawable.ic_back), contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.adjust_back))
                }
            }
            Text(
                title,
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium,
                maxLines = 1,
                overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis,
                modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
            )
            actions()
            Spacer(Modifier.width(4.dp))
            DonePill(onClick = onDone)
        }
        Column(
            Modifier.padding(start = 16.dp, end = 16.dp, top = 2.dp, bottom = 12.dp),
            verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(10.dp),
            content = content,
        )
    }
}

/** Project frame shape; the preview letterboxes to match. "Original" follows the first clip. */
@Composable
fun RatioTool(
    selected: AspectRatio,
    /** Width:height that [AspectRatio.ORIGINAL] resolves to, for its glyph. */
    originalRatio: Pair<Int, Int>,
    onSelected: (AspectRatio) -> Unit,
    onDone: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
    ToolPanel(stringResource(R.string.ratio_title), onDone, modifier) {
        Row(Modifier.horizontalScroll(rememberScrollState()), horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
            AspectRatio.entries.forEach { ratio ->
                val shape = if (ratio == AspectRatio.ORIGINAL) originalRatio else ratio.widthRatio to ratio.heightRatio
                PreCutChip(
                    label = ratio.label(),
                    selected = ratio == selected,
                    onClick = { onSelected(ratio) },
                    leading = { RatioGlyph(shape.first, shape.second, if (ratio == selected) OnAccentContainer else TextPrimary) },
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

@Composable
private fun AspectRatio.label(): String = when (this) {
    AspectRatio.ORIGINAL -> stringResource(R.string.ratio_original)
    AspectRatio.RATIO_235_100 -> "2.35:1"
    AspectRatio.RATIO_185_100 -> "1.85:1"
    AspectRatio.RATIO_9_19_5 -> "9:19.5"
    else -> "$widthRatio:$heightRatio"
}

@Composable
private fun RatioGlyph(width: Int, height: Int, color: Color) {
    val longSide = 16f
    val scale = longSide / maxOf(width, height, 1)
    Box(
        Modifier
            .size((width * scale).dp, (height * scale).dp)
            .border(1.5.dp, color, RoundedCornerShape(2.dp)),
    )
}

private val TileShape = RoundedCornerShape(8.dp)
private val TileSize = 60.dp

/** A filter tile: the clip's frame graded by [filterId] (ungraded when null), with its name. */
@Composable
fun FilterTile(
    label: String,
    filterId: String?,
    baseKey: ThumbnailKey?,
    loader: ThumbnailLoader,
    thumbnailer: LookThumbnailer,
    selected: Boolean,
    onClick: () -> Unit,
) {
    val image by produceState<Bitmap?>(null, baseKey, filterId) {
        val base = baseKey?.let { loader.load(it) } ?: return@produceState
        value = if (filterId == null) base else thumbnailer.graded(base, filterId) ?: base
    }
    TileFrame(label, selected, onClick) {
        image?.let { Image(it.asImageBitmap(), contentDescription = null, contentScale = ContentScale.Crop, modifier = Modifier.matchParentSize()) }
    }
}

/** A tile with an icon instead of a picture (e.g. "Import .cube"). */
@Composable
fun IconTile(label: String, icon: Int, onClick: () -> Unit, selected: Boolean = false) {
    TileFrame(label, selected, onClick) {
        Icon(painterResource(icon), contentDescription = null, modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.Center))
    }
}

@Composable
private fun TileFrame(label: String, selected: Boolean, onClick: () -> Unit, content: @Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit) {
    val accent = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary
    Column(
        horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(4.dp),
        modifier = Modifier.width(TileSize).clickable(onClick = onClick),
    ) {
        Box(
            Modifier
                .size(TileSize)
                .clip(TileShape)

private val TileShape = RoundedCornerShape(8.dp)

/** A filter tile: the clip's frame graded by [filterId] (ungraded when null), with its name. */
@Composable
fun FilterTile(
    label: String,
    filterId: String?,
    baseKey: ThumbnailKey?,
    loader: ThumbnailLoader,
    thumbnailer: LookThumbnailer,
    selected: Boolean,
    onClick: () -> Unit,
) {
    val image by produceState<Bitmap?>(null, baseKey, filterId) {
        val base = baseKey?.let { loader.load(it) } ?: return@produceState
        value = if (filterId == null) base else thumbnailer.graded(base, filterId) ?: base
    }
    TileFrame(label, selected, onClick) {
        image?.let { Image(it.asImageBitmap(), contentDescription = null, contentScale = ContentScale.Crop, modifier = Modifier.matchParentSize()) }
    }
}

/** A tile with an icon instead of a picture (e.g. "Import .cube"). */
@Composable
fun IconTile(label: String, icon: Int, onClick: () -> Unit, selected: Boolean = false) {

    }
}

private fun TileFrame(label: String, selected: Boolean, onClick: () -> Unit, content: @Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit) {

            color = if (selected) TextPrimary else TextSecondary,
            textAlign = TextAlign.Center,
            maxLines = 2,
            overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis,
        )
    }
}

/** Transform (T-15): Fit/Fill (each starts over), a readout of the transform, and the gesture hint. */
@Composable
fun TransformTool(fit: FrameFit, transform: ClipTransform, onFit: (FrameFit) -> Unit, onReset: () -> Unit, onDone: () -> Unit) {
    ToolPanel(
        stringResource(R.string.tool_transform),
        onDone,
        actions = {
            AccentTextButton(
                stringResource(R.string.action_reset),
                onClick = onReset,
                enabled = fit != FrameFit.FIT || !transform.isIdentity,
                color = TextSecondary,
            )
        },
    ) {
        Row(Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically, horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
            val plain = transform.isIdentity
            PreCutChip(stringResource(R.string.transform_fit), selected = plain && fit == FrameFit.FIT, onClick = { onFit(FrameFit.FIT) }, icon = R.drawable.ic_fit)
            PreCutChip(stringResource(R.string.transform_fill), selected = plain && fit == FrameFit.FILL, onClick = { onFit(FrameFit.FILL) }, icon = R.drawable.ic_crop_free)
            Text(
                stringResource(
                    R.string.transform_readout,
                    (transform.scale * 100).roundToInt(),
                    transform.rotationDegrees.roundToInt(),
                    (transform.offsetX * 100).roundToInt(),
                    (transform.offsetY * 100).roundToInt(),
                ),
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall.tabular(),
                color = TextSecondary,
                maxLines = 1,
                modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
            )
        }
        Text(stringResource(R.string.transform_hint), style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall, color = TextSecondary)
    }
}

package com.savie.precut.ui.editor.crop

import android.graphics.Bitmap
import android.graphics.Matrix
import androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas
import androidx.compose.foundation.Image
import androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.awaitEachGesture
import androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.awaitFirstDown
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.BoxWithConstraints
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.offset
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.size
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.produceState
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.rememberUpdatedState
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Offset
import androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Rect
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.asImageBitmap
import androidx.compose.ui.input.pointer.pointerInput
import androidx.compose.ui.input.pointer.positionChange
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalDensity
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.IntOffset
import com.savie.precut.media.ThumbnailKey
import com.savie.precut.media.ThumbnailLoader
import com.savie.precut.model.frame.CropRect
import com.savie.precut.model.frame.FrameGeometry
import kotlin.math.min
import kotlin.math.roundToInt

/**
 * Crop mode's picture (T-12b): a still of the clip at the playhead, mirrored and turned as in the
 * draft, with the crop rectangle on top. Corners resize (keeping a locked ratio), edges resize when
 * free, and dragging inside moves it.
 */
@Composable
fun CropPreview(
    frameKey: ThumbnailKey,
    loader: ThumbnailLoader,
    mirrored: Boolean,
    rotationDegrees: Int,
    crop: CropRect,
    lockedAspect: Float?,
    onChange: (CropRect) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
    val source by produceState<Bitmap?>(null, frameKey) { value = loader.load(frameKey, cache = false) }
    val picture = remember(source, mirrored, rotationDegrees) { source?.let { upright(it, mirrored, rotationDegrees) } }
    BoxWithConstraints(modifier) {
        val bitmap = picture ?: return@BoxWithConstraints
        val boxW = constraints.maxWidth.toFloat()
        val boxH = constraints.maxHeight.toFloat()
        val scale = min(boxW / bitmap.width, boxH / bitmap.height)
        val area = Rect(Offset((boxW - bitmap.width * scale) / 2, (boxH - bitmap.height * scale) / 2), androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Size(bitmap.width * scale, bitmap.height * scale))
        val density = LocalDensity.current
        val image = remember(bitmap) { bitmap.asImageBitmap() }
        Image(
            image,
            contentDescription = null,
            modifier = Modifier
                .offset { IntOffset(area.left.roundToInt(), area.top.roundToInt()) }
                .size(with(density) { area.width.toDp() }, with(density) { area.height.toDp() }),
        )
        val currentCrop by rememberUpdatedState(crop)
        val currentAspect by rememberUpdatedState(lockedAspect)
        val currentArea by rememberUpdatedState(area)
        val pictureAspect = bitmap.width.toFloat() / bitmap.height
        Canvas(
            Modifier
                .matchParentSize()
                .pointerInput(pictureAspect) {
                    awaitEachGesture {
                        val down = awaitFirstDown()
                        val start = currentCrop
                        val handle = handleAt(down.position, start.toPx(currentArea), currentAspect != null, 28f * density.density)
                            ?: return@awaitEachGesture
                        var total = Offset.Zero
                        do {
                            val event = awaitPointerEvent()
                            val change = event.changes.firstOrNull { it.id == down.id } ?: break
                            total += change.positionChange()
                            change.consume()
                            onChange(FrameGeometry.dragCrop(start, handle, total.x / currentArea.width, total.y / currentArea.height, currentAspect, pictureAspect))
                        } while (change.pressed)
                    }
                },
        ) {
            drawCropFrame(crop.toPx(area))
        }
    }
}

/** [source] flipped left–right (when [mirrored]) and then turned clockwise, as Media3 does. */
private fun upright(source: Bitmap, mirrored: Boolean, rotationDegrees: Int): Bitmap {
    if (!mirrored && rotationDegrees % 360 == 0) return source
    val matrix = Matrix().apply {
        if (mirrored) postScale(-1f, 1f)
        postRotate(rotationDegrees.toFloat())
    }
    return Bitmap.createBitmap(source, 0, 0, source.width, source.height, matrix, true)
}

private fun CropRect.toPx(area: Rect) = Rect(
    area.left + left * area.width,
    area.top + top * area.height,
    area.left + right * area.width,
    area.top + bottom * area.height,
)

/** The handle under [point]: corners first, then edges (free ratio only), then inside to move. */
private fun handleAt(point: Offset, crop: Rect, locked: Boolean, slopPx: Float): FrameGeometry.CropHandle? {
    fun near(a: Float, b: Float) = kotlin.math.abs(a - b) <= slopPx
    val left = near(point.x, crop.left)
    val right = near(point.x, crop.right)
    val top = near(point.y, crop.top)
    val bottom = near(point.y, crop.bottom)
    val withinX = point.x in crop.left - slopPx..crop.right + slopPx
    val withinY = point.y in crop.top - slopPx..crop.bottom + slopPx
    return when {
        left && top -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.TOP_LEFT
        right && top -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.TOP_RIGHT
        left && bottom -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.BOTTOM_LEFT
        right && bottom -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.BOTTOM_RIGHT
        !locked && left && withinY -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.LEFT
        !locked && right && withinY -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.RIGHT
        !locked && top && withinX -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.TOP
        !locked && bottom && withinX -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.BOTTOM
        crop.contains(point) -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.MOVE
        else -> null
    }
}

package com.savie.precut.ui.editor.crop

import androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Offset
import androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Rect
import androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Size
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.drawscope.DrawScope
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.drawscope.Stroke
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp

/** Dims outside [crop], then draws its 1.5 dp border, thirds grid and 4 dp corner marks (T-12b). */
fun DrawScope.drawCropFrame(crop: Rect) {
    val dim = Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.62f)
    drawRect(dim, Offset.Zero, Size(size.width, crop.top))
    drawRect(dim, Offset(0f, crop.bottom), Size(size.width, size.height - crop.bottom))
    drawRect(dim, Offset(0f, crop.top), Size(crop.left, crop.height))
    drawRect(dim, Offset(crop.right, crop.top), Size(size.width - crop.right, crop.height))

    val grid = Color.White.copy(alpha = 0.55f)
    val hair = 1.dp.toPx()
    for (i in 1..2) {
        val x = crop.left + crop.width * i / 3
        val y = crop.top + crop.height * i / 3
        drawLine(grid, Offset(x, crop.top), Offset(x, crop.bottom), hair)
        drawLine(grid, Offset(crop.left, y), Offset(crop.right, y), hair)
    }
    drawRect(Color.White, crop.topLeft, crop.size, style = Stroke(1.5.dp.toPx()))

    val thick = 4.dp.toPx()
    val arm = 22.dp.toPx()
    val inset = thick / 2 - 4.dp.toPx() + thick / 2
    listOf(
        Triple(crop.topLeft, 1f, 1f),
        Triple(crop.topRight, -1f, 1f),
        Triple(crop.bottomLeft, 1f, -1f),
        Triple(crop.bottomRight, -1f, -1f),
    ).forEach { (corner, sx, sy) ->
        val c = Offset(corner.x - sx * (thick / 2 - inset), corner.y - sy * (thick / 2 - inset))
        drawLine(Color.White, c, Offset(c.x + sx * arm, c.y), thick)
        drawLine(Color.White, c, Offset(c.x, c.y + sy * arm), thick)
    }
}

import androidx.compose.ui.unit.IntOffset
import com.savie.precut.media.ThumbnailKey
import com.savie.precut.media.ThumbnailLoader
import com.savie.precut.model.frame.CropRect
import com.savie.precut.model.frame.FrameGeometry
import kotlin.math.min
import kotlin.math.roundToInt

/**
 * Crop mode's picture (T-12b): a still of the clip at the playhead, mirrored and turned as in the
 * draft, with the crop rectangle on top. Corners resize (keeping a locked ratio), edges resize when
 * free, and dragging inside moves it.
 */
@Composable
fun CropPreview(
    frameKey: ThumbnailKey,
    loader: ThumbnailLoader,
    mirrored: Boolean,
    rotationDegrees: Int,
    crop: CropRect,
    lockedAspect: Float?,
    onChange: (CropRect) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
    val source by produceState<Bitmap?>(null, frameKey) { value = loader.load(frameKey, cache = false) }
    val picture = remember(source, mirrored, rotationDegrees) { source?.let { upright(it, mirrored, rotationDegrees) } }
    BoxWithConstraints(modifier) {
        val bitmap = picture ?: return@BoxWithConstraints
        val boxW = constraints.maxWidth.toFloat()
        val boxH = constraints.maxHeight.toFloat()
        val scale = min(boxW / bitmap.width, boxH / bitmap.height)
        val area = Rect(Offset((boxW - bitmap.width * scale) / 2, (boxH - bitmap.height * scale) / 2), androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Size(bitmap.width * scale, bitmap.height * scale))
        val density = LocalDensity.current
        val image = remember(bitmap) { bitmap.asImageBitmap() }
        Image(
            image,
            contentDescription = null,
            modifier = Modifier
                .offset { IntOffset(area.left.roundToInt(), area.top.roundToInt()) }
                .size(with(density) { area.width.toDp() }, with(density) { area.height.toDp() }),
        )
        val currentCrop by rememberUpdatedState(crop)
        val currentAspect by rememberUpdatedState(lockedAspect)
        val currentArea by rememberUpdatedState(area)
        val pictureAspect = bitmap.width.toFloat() / bitmap.height
        Canvas(
            Modifier
                .matchParentSize()
                .pointerInput(pictureAspect) {
                    awaitEachGesture {
                        val down = awaitFirstDown()
                        val start = currentCrop
                        val handle = handleAt(down.position, start.toPx(currentArea), currentAspect != null, 28f * density.density)
                            ?: return@awaitEachGesture
                        var total = Offset.Zero
                        do {
                            val event = awaitPointerEvent()
                            val change = event.changes.firstOrNull { it.id == down.id } ?: break
                            total += change.positionChange()
                            change.consume()
                            onChange(FrameGeometry.dragCrop(start, handle, total.x / currentArea.width, total.y / currentArea.height, currentAspect, pictureAspect))
                        } while (change.pressed)
                    }
                },
        ) {
            drawCropFrame(crop.toPx(area))
        }
    }
}

/** [source] flipped left–right (when [mirrored]) and then turned clockwise, as Media3 does. */
private fun upright(source: Bitmap, mirrored: Boolean, rotationDegrees: Int): Bitmap {
    if (!mirrored && rotationDegrees % 360 == 0) return source
    val matrix = Matrix().apply {
        if (mirrored) postScale(-1f, 1f)
        postRotate(rotationDegrees.toFloat())
    }
    return Bitmap.createBitmap(source, 0, 0, source.width, source.height, matrix, true)
}

private fun CropRect.toPx(area: Rect) = Rect(
    area.left + left * area.width,
    area.top + top * area.height,
    area.left + right * area.width,
    area.top + bottom * area.height,
)

/** The handle under [point]: corners first, then edges (free ratio only), then inside to move. */
private fun handleAt(point: Offset, crop: Rect, locked: Boolean, slopPx: Float): FrameGeometry.CropHandle? {
    fun near(a: Float, b: Float) = kotlin.math.abs(a - b) <= slopPx
    val left = near(point.x, crop.left)
    val right = near(point.x, crop.right)
    val top = near(point.y, crop.top)
    val bottom = near(point.y, crop.bottom)
    val withinX = point.x in crop.left - slopPx..crop.right + slopPx
    val withinY = point.y in crop.top - slopPx..crop.bottom + slopPx
    return when {
        left && top -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.TOP_LEFT
        right && top -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.TOP_RIGHT
        left && bottom -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.BOTTOM_LEFT
        right && bottom -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.BOTTOM_RIGHT
        !locked && left && withinY -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.LEFT
        !locked && right && withinY -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.RIGHT
        !locked && top && withinX -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.TOP
        !locked && bottom && withinX -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.BOTTOM
        crop.contains(point) -> FrameGeometry.CropHandle.MOVE
        else -> null
    }
}

package com.savie.precut.ui.editor.crop

import androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Offset
import androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Rect
import androidx.compose.ui.geometry.Size
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.drawscope.DrawScope
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.drawscope.Stroke
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp

/** Dims outside [crop], then draws its 1.5 dp border, thirds grid and 4 dp corner marks (T-12b). */
fun DrawScope.drawCropFrame(crop: Rect) {
    val dim = Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.62f)
    drawRect(dim, Offset.Zero, Size(size.width, crop.top))
    drawRect(dim, Offset(0f, crop.bottom), Size(size.width, size.height - crop.bottom))
    drawRect(dim, Offset(0f, crop.top), Size(crop.left, crop.height))
    drawRect(dim, Offset(crop.right, crop.top), Size(size.width - crop.right, crop.height))

    val grid = Color.White.copy(alpha = 0.55f)
    val hair = 1.dp.toPx()
    for (i in 1..2) {
        val x = crop.left + crop.width * i / 3
        val y = crop.top + crop.height * i / 3
        drawLine(grid, Offset(x, crop.top), Offset(x, crop.bottom), hair)
        drawLine(grid, Offset(crop.left, y), Offset(crop.right, y), hair)
    }
    drawRect(Color.White, crop.topLeft, crop.size, style = Stroke(1.5.dp.toPx()))

    val thick = 4.dp.toPx()
    val arm = 22.dp.toPx()
    val inset = thick / 2 - 4.dp.toPx() + thick / 2
    listOf(
        Triple(crop.topLeft, 1f, 1f),
        Triple(crop.topRight, -1f, 1f),
        Triple(crop.bottomLeft, 1f, -1f),
        Triple(crop.bottomRight, -1f, -1f),
    ).forEach { (corner, sx, sy) ->
        val c = Offset(corner.x - sx * (thick / 2 - inset), corner.y - sy * (thick / 2 - inset))
        drawLine(Color.White, c, Offset(c.x + sx * arm, c.y), thick)
        drawLine(Color.White, c, Offset(c.x, c.y + sy * arm), thick)
    }
}

package com.savie.precut.ui.editor

import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import com.savie.precut.media.ThumbnailKey
import com.savie.precut.model.Clip

import com.savie.precut.ui.editor.tools.EditTool
import com.savie.precut.ui.editor.tools.OpacityTool
import com.savie.precut.ui.editor.tools.TransformTool

/** The Edit, Transform, Opacity and Canvas panels for [clip]. */
@Composable
fun FramePanels(clip: Clip, tool: EditorTool, viewModel: EditorViewModel) {
    val frame = viewModel.frame
    val close = viewModel::onToolClosed
    when (tool) {
        EditorTool.EDIT -> EditTool(onCrop = frame::onCropStart, onMirror = frame::onMirror, onRotate = frame::onRotate, onDone = close)
        EditorTool.TRANSFORM -> TransformTool(clip.fit, clip.transform, onFit = frame::onFit, onReset = frame::onResetTransform, onDone = close)
        EditorTool.OPACITY -> OpacityTool(clip.opacity, onLive = frame::onOpacityLive, onChanged = frame::onOpacityDone, onDone = close)
        EditorTool.CANVAS -> {
            val actions = remember(frame) {
                object : CanvasActions {

package com.savie.precut.ui.editor

import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable

import com.savie.precut.ui.editor.tools.TransformTool

/** The Edit, Transform, Opacity and Canvas panels for [clip]. */
@Composable
fun FramePanels(clip: Clip, tool: EditorTool, viewModel: EditorViewModel) {
    val frame = viewModel.frame
    val close = viewModel::onToolClosed
    when (tool) {
        EditorTool.EDIT -> EditTool(onCrop = frame::onCropStart, onMirror = frame::onMirror, onRotate = frame::onRotate, onDone = close)
        EditorTool.TRANSFORM -> TransformTool(clip.fit, clip.transform, onFit = frame::onFit, onReset = frame::onResetTransform, onDone = close)
        EditorTool.OPACITY -> OpacityTool(clip.opacity, onLive = frame::onOpacityLive, onChanged = frame::onOpacityDone, onDone = close)
        EditorTool.CANVAS -> {
            val actions = remember(frame) {
                object : CanvasActions {
                    override fun onCanvas(canvas: ClipCanvas) = frame.onCanvas(canvas)
                    override fun onApplyAll() = frame.onCanvasApplyAll()
                    override fun onPickImage() = frame.onPickCanvasImage()
                }

            val key = remember(clip.uri, clip.trimStartMs) {
                ThumbnailKey(clip.uri, clip.type, clip.trimStartMs, TILE_FRAME_HEIGHT_PX, if (clip.type == ClipType.IMAGE) clip.sourceRotationDegrees else 0)
            }
            CanvasTool(clip.canvas, key, viewModel.thumbnails, actions, onDone = close)
        }
        else -> Unit
    }
}

    assert item in s, item

s=s.rstrip('\n')+'''
- **2026-10-14 — Phase 8B frame:** per clip, Media3 runs mirror + 90° turns (`ScaleAndRotateTransformation`) → `Crop` → `CanvasEffect`, PreCut's own GL pass that places the clip (Fit/Fill, then the user transform), applies opacity and draws the canvas (colour, a 1/8-size separable-Gaussian blur of the clip, or a picture). Media3's `GaussianBlurWithFrameOverlaid` can't move or rotate the sharp frame, so it wasn't usable. Plain clips (fitted, opaque, on black) keep `Presentation`, so old projects render exactly as before. The crop is stored on the mirrored/rotated picture and turns/flips with it; Mirror always flips left–right on screen (on a sideways clip that's a source flip plus 180°). One Mirror control as in the design: an up–down flip is Mirror + Rotate 180°.
- **2026-10-14 — Live preview for transform and opacity:** `CompositionPlayer` can't change effects while playing, and rebuilding per finger movement is too slow. While Transform or Opacity is open, the preview marks that clip "live": its `CanvasEffect` reads `LiveFrames` (a value set only by the preview) every frame, and the paused frame is redrawn by seeking in scrubbing mode, alternating between the position and 1 ms beside it, because ExoPlayer ignores a seek to the same millisecond. On release the edit is committed and the preview rebuilt through `CompositionBuilder`; export never sets a live clip, and a live clip renders exactly as it would without the mark. **Verify on device** that the picture follows the finger smoothly.
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='docs/design/DESIGN.md'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('| T-12 – T-15 | Edit/crop, Canvas, Opacity, Transform | Phase 8B |','| T-12 – T-15 | Edit/crop, Canvas, Opacity, Transform | `ui/editor/tools/{EditTool,CanvasTool,OpacityTool,TransformTool}.kt`, `ui/editor/crop/`, `ui/editor/preview/ClipTransformOverlay.kt` |')

EOF

content.text:
Phase 8B (Frame) is built: crop, mirror, rotate, transform on the preview, canvas and opacity. It builds with no warnings and all unit tests pass, including 17 new ones. The four 8B items are ticked in [PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md), with two new entries in the decisions log. I haven't seen any of it run on a device yet, so the steps below are the first real check.

**What's new**
- **Toolbar:** Rotate is now **Edit** (Crop, Mirror, Rotate), and **Canvas** and **Opacity** are added.
- **Crop mode:** it takes over the screen and works on a still of the frame under the playhead.
  - Corners resize, edges resize when the ratio is Free, and dragging inside moves the rectangle.
  - Ratio chips: Free, Original, 9:16, 16:9, 1:1, 4:5. Mirror and Rotate are available inside crop mode too.
  - ✓ saves everything as one undo step; ✕ discards it.
- **Transform:** with a clip selected, its outline shows on the preview.
  - Drag moves it, pinch scales, and twisting or the bottom handle rotates it.
  - It snaps to the centre lines and to right angles with a haptic tick, and shows an angle chip while turning.
  - The panel has Fit, Fill, Reset and a readout.
- **Canvas:** Colour (swatches plus the colour picker), Blur (None, Light, Medium, Strong, Max) or Image (gallery photo, or the Dots, Stripes, Sand and Dusk patterns drawn in code), with Apply to all.
- **Opacity:** a 0–100% slider with Reset.
- **Behind the scenes:** clips with default settings still take Media3's standard path, so existing projects render exactly as before. Photos used as canvases are kept by the unused-media cleanup.

**Not checked on a device yet**
- **Live follow:** while you drag, pinch or move the opacity slider, the preview should follow your finger. This relies on a workaround: ExoPlayer ignores a seek to the same millisecond, so the redraw alternates between the playhead and 1 ms beside it. If the picture lags, the fallback is that the outline follows live and the video catches up when you let go.
- **The first gesture after selecting a clip** has to rebuild the preview, so that one may lag briefly.
- **Tiles on Android 8–11:** the blur tiles in the Canvas panel won't look blurred there, because Compose only supports blur on Android 12 and up. The exported video is still blurred.
- **Covers ignore frame edits:** the project cover and the Projects-screen thumbnail use the raw frame, without crop or transform.

**Device test steps**
1. **Crop:**
   - Select a clip, tap Edit → Crop and choose 1:1. Drag a corner (the square should stay square), then drag inside to move it, then tap ✓.
   - Undo should restore the uncropped clip in one step.
2. **Mirror and rotate:** tap Mirror, then Rotate; the picture should flip left–right and then turn 90°. Rotate once more and tap Mirror again: it should still flip left–right on screen. If the clip was cropped, the crop should follow the picture.

Gaps on purpose: the Speed **Curve** tab shows "Soon" (Phase 8C); Projects has no Settings button (H-09, Phase 12); importing (H-07) shows an indeterminate bar with no count or Cancel, because `MediaImporter` reports neither progress nor cancellation yet. The `material-icons-core` dependency is gone; every icon is a Material Symbols drawable.

- **2026-10-14 — Phase 8B frame:** per clip, Media3 runs mirror + 90° turns (`ScaleAndRotateTransformation`) → `Crop` → `CanvasEffect`, PreCut's own GL pass that places the clip (Fit/Fill, then the user transform), applies opacity and draws the canvas (colour, a 1/8-size separable-Gaussian blur of the clip, or a picture). Media3's `GaussianBlurWithFrameOverlaid` can't move or rotate the sharp frame, so it wasn't usable. Plain clips (fitted, opaque, on black) keep `Presentation`, so old projects render exactly as before. The crop is stored on the mirrored/rotated picture and turns/flips with it; Mirror always flips left–right on screen (on a sideways clip that's a source flip plus 180°). One Mirror control as in the design: an up–down flip is Mirror + Rotate 180°.

- **2026-10-14 — Live preview for transform and opacity:** `CompositionPlayer` can't change effects while playing, and rebuilding per finger movement is too slow. While Transform or Opacity is open, the preview marks that clip "live": its `CanvasEffect` reads `LiveFrames` (a value set only by the preview) every frame, and the paused frame is redrawn by seeking in scrubbing mode, alternating between the position and 1 ms beside it, because ExoPlayer ignores a seek to the same millisecond. On release the edit is committed and the preview rebuilt through `CompositionBuilder`; export never sets a live clip, and a live clip renders exactly as it would without the mark. **Verify on device** that the picture follows the finger smoothly.

content.text:
I've fixed both problems, but haven't tested on a device. No phone was connected over adb, so I couldn't read the crash log; I found both causes in our code and Media3's source. The app builds with no warnings and the unit tests pass. These two classes need Android to run, so there are no new automated tests for them.

**1. The clip disappeared after closing the app.** When you pick a video, the app asks Android to keep access to that file permanently. Some pickers refuse, and the code ignored the refusal. Access then lasted only until the app closed, and on reopening the clip showed as missing.

**The fix** ([MediaImporter.kt](app/src/main/java/com/savie/precut/media/MediaImporter.kt)): after asking, the app now checks that access was actually kept. If it wasn't, it copies the file into the app's own storage and uses the copy. That copy is kept as long as a project uses it. Music files get the same treatment. I also made the media check work out a file's type from its extension when Android doesn't report one. Before this, camera captures and copied files could be rejected as unsupported.

**2. The crash when moving the blank clip.** A missing clip is left out of the preview. When every clip is missing, the preview player is never given anything to play. Dragging on the timeline still told it to jump to a position, and Media3's player crashes when asked to do that before it has ever had something to play.

**The fix** ([PreviewController.kt](app/src/main/java/com/savie/precut/media/PreviewController.kt)): the preview now ignores jumping, scrubbing and play while it has nothing to play. Jumps are also limited to the preview's length, because the timeline is longer than the preview when media is missing.

Both are recorded in the decisions log in PLAN.md.

**This won't bring back clips that are already broken.** Projects saved before the fix still point to files the app can no longer read. Use **Replace** on the missing clip, or **Remove all** in the missing-media banner, to repair them.

**Device test steps**
1. Create a new project from the gallery and make an edit. Then fully close the app: swipe it away from recents, or Force stop in Settings.
2. Reopen the project. The clip should play, with no missing-media banner.
3. Repeat with a clip added from the editor's **+** button, and with music added under Audio.
4. Open one of the old broken projects and drag the blank clip and the timeline. It should no longer crash. Then use Replace to fix the clip.

If it still crashes, connect the phone with USB debugging on and tell me, so I can read the exact error.

While reading the source I also found that Media3 1.11.1 has a built-in `experimentalRedrawLastFrame()`. It could replace the 1 ms seek workaround behind Phase 8B's live transform. Since that works well on your phone, I've left it alone.

Suggested commit:
```
fix: keep picked media readable after restart; don't seek an empty preview
```

Once you've confirmed the fix, I'll write the plan for Phase 8C (transitions, animations, speed curves, freeze frame, reverse).

content.text:
Done checking. The speed provider gets source time measured from the clip's trimmed start, which suits curves defined over the clip. Here's the Phase 8C plan for your approval; nothing is coded yet.

## Phase 8C — Motion and time: plan

I'd split it into two stops, each with its own device check:
- **8C-1:** transitions, animations and freeze frame. These are effect work that fits the existing setup.
- **8C-2:** speed curves and reverse. These change timeline timing and add a background rendering job, so they're riskier.

### Where Media3 differs from the plan
1. **Media3 has no reverse.** I'd make the reversed copy with our own pipeline:
   - **Video:** Transformer re-encodes the clip's trimmed range with every frame as a keyframe. Then `MediaCodec` decodes those frames from last to first, straight into an encoder with new timestamps.
   - **Audio:** decoded to a temporary raw-audio file, read backwards and re-encoded.
   - I'll prototype this first, as the plan says.
2. **Speed curves:** `CompositionPlayer` supports a varying `SpeedProvider` in preview and in export. Media3 only accepts speeds that change in steps, so each curve becomes about 40 steps across the clip. The timeline maths uses the same steps, so lengths, splitting and the playhead all agree with Media3.
3. **Transitions in T-16:** Dissolve, Slide, Push and Wipe make neighbouring clips overlap, which the plan puts in Phase 9. I'd leave them out of the grid until then rather than show items that don't work.
4. **Motion blur** (a stretch goal) stays for later; it isn't in this phase.

### 8C-1: transitions, animations, freeze frame

**Transitions (T-16)**
- **Timeline:** each join between clips gets the design's diamond marker; tapping it opens the Transition panel. A selected marker turns accent, with a band showing how long the transition lasts.
- **Panel:**
  - Tiles: None, Fade black, Fade white, Flash, Zoom in, Zoom out, Blur, Glitch, Spin.
  - A duration slider from 0.1 to 2 s (default 0.5 s), limited by the shorter of the two clips.
  - Apply to all, which sets every join.
- **Model:** `Clip.transitionOut` holds the type and duration. It follows the clip when it's split (to the second half) or duplicated, and it's ignored on the last clip.
- **Rendering:** these transitions don't overlap clips, so the total length doesn't change. The first clip plays the first half of the effect over its last part, and the next clip plays the second half over its first part. For example, with Fade black the first clip fades out and the next fades in.
  - A new `TransitionEffect` GL pass runs on each clip after its canvas.
  - It's active only in that clip's first or last moments, worked out from the clip's start time on the timeline (Media3 gives effects timeline time).

**Animations (T-17, T-17b)**
- **Panel:** tabs In, Out and Combo.
  - **In and Out:** Fade, Zoom, Slide up, Slide down, Slide left, Slide right, Spin, Bounce, Shake, each with a duration.
  - **Combo:** Fade (pulse), Zoom in-out, Slide (swing), Rock, Spin, Bounce, Shake, with a speed setting from 0.5x to 2x. A combo loops for the whole clip and replaces In and Out.
  - Tapping a tile applies it and plays that part of the clip once as a preview.
- **Model:** `animationIn`, `animationOut` and `animationCombo`. The animation curves (eased scale, offset, rotation and opacity over time) live in `model/` as pure code.
- **Rendering:** the existing `CanvasEffect` adds the animation on top of your transform for each frame. The clip moves over its own canvas, as in CapCut.

**Freeze frame (T-18)**
- It splits the clip at the playhead and inserts a 3 s photo of that exact frame, taken from the original file rather than the low-res preview copy.
- The photo keeps the clip's look, crop, transform and canvas, and any transition moves to the second half.
- Snackbar: "Freeze frame added · 3s" with Undo. Everything happens in one undo step.
- Freeze images are saved in `files/freezes`, which the media cleanup keeps for as long as a project uses them.

**Toolbar:** Animation, Freeze and (in 8C-2) Reverse are added in the design's order (E-04b).

### 8C-2: speed curves and reverse

**Speed curves (T-03)**
- The Speed panel's Curve tab (currently "Soon") gets these tiles: Custom, Montage, Hero, Bullet, Jump cut, Flash in, Flash out.
- **Graph:** speed from 0.1x to 10x on a log scale over the clip's length. You drag points; tap adds one and long-press removes one. A readout shows the length change, for example "5.6s → 4.1s".
- **Model:** `Clip.speedCurve`, with points stored as a fraction of the clip's length.
  - One step map drives the clip's length and the conversions between timeline time and source time.
  - Split, trim, fades, text clamping and playhead mapping all follow from it.
  - Splitting gives each half its part of the curve, and Normal clears the curve.
  - Photos have no curves.
- **Media:** a `CurveSpeedProvider` built from those same steps. Keep pitch is supported, and the 60 fps cap applies when the curve goes above 1x.

**Reverse (T-19, T-19b)**
- **Dialog:** "Reversing clip… 45%" with a time estimate and Cancel, then a snackbar "Clip reversed" with Undo.
- **Model:** reversing swaps the clip's media for the reversed file and remembers the original, so reversing again restores it straight away. Undo works as normal.
  - Everything else (thumbnails, preview copies, export, missing-media checks) works unchanged.
  - A reversed clip can only be trimmed shorter. To make it longer: undo the reverse, trim, then reverse again.
- **Storage:** reversed files are cached in `files/reversed`, keyed by file and range, and the media cleanup keeps them.
- They're made at up to 1080p, matching today's export.

### Tests
- **8C-1:**
  - animation and transition maths: start and end windows, clamping, easing
  - transition behaviour on split, move and delete
  - the freeze reducer (split + insert + carried settings)
  - spec mapping
  - old drafts load unchanged
- **8C-2:**
  - step-map length and conversions in both directions, checked against Media3's own length formula
  - curve split and trim
  - preset shapes
  - reverse and restore in the model
  - spec mapping

### Acceptance
- **8C-1:** two transitions, an In and an Out animation, a combo and a freeze frame look the same in preview and export, with total length unchanged except for the freeze.
- **8C-2:** a Hero curve and a reversed clip (with its sound reversed) match between preview and export, and the timeline length matches the exported file.

package com.savie.precut.ui.editor.timeline

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.key
import androidx.compose.ui.zIndex
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.Dp
import com.savie.precut.media.ThumbnailLoader
import com.savie.precut.model.Project
import com.savie.precut.model.clipStartTimesMs

/** Clips side by side, each as wide as its timeline duration. [visiblePx] is in timeline px. */
@Composable
fun ClipStrip(
    project: Project,
    selectedClipId: String?,
    multiIds: Set<String>,
    multiSelectMode: Boolean,
    missingIds: Set<String>,
    pxPerMs: Float,
    clipHeight: Dp,
    visiblePx: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>,
    loader: ThumbnailLoader,
    snapTargets: () -> List<Long>,
    snapThresholdMs: Long,
    onTrim: (clipId: String, trimStartMs: Long, trimEndMs: Long) -> Unit,
) {
    Row {
        val starts = project.clipStartTimesMs()
        project.clips.forEachIndexed { index, clip ->
            val clipStartPx = TimelineGeometry.msToPx(starts[index], pxPerMs)
            // key(): after a reorder each clip keeps its own state (drag offsets, tiles).
            key(clip.id) {
                // The selected clip's handles reach over its neighbours, so it's drawn on top.
                ClipView(
                    clip = clip,
                    clipStartMs = starts[index],
                    pxPerMs = pxPerMs,
                    height = clipHeight,
                    look = ClipLook(
                        selected = clip.id == selectedClipId,
                        multiSelected = clip.id in multiIds,
                        multiSelectMode = multiSelectMode,
                        soundOff = clip.muted || clip.volume == 0f || project.originalAudioMuted,
                        missing = clip.id in missingIds,
                    ),
                    visiblePx = (visiblePx.start - clipStartPx)..(visiblePx.endInclusive - clipStartPx),
                    loader = loader,
                    snapTargets = snapTargets,
                    snapThresholdMs = snapThresholdMs,
                    onTrim = { start, end -> onTrim(clip.id, start, end) },
                    modifier = Modifier.zIndex(if (clip.id == selectedClipId) 1f else 0f),
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

import com.savie.precut.media.ThumbnailLoader
import com.savie.precut.model.Project
import com.savie.precut.model.clipStartTimesMs

/** Clips side by side, each as wide as its timeline duration. [visiblePx] is in timeline px. */
@Composable
fun ClipStrip(
    project: Project,
    selectedClipId: String?,
    multiIds: Set<String>,
    multiSelectMode: Boolean,
    missingIds: Set<String>,
    pxPerMs: Float,
    clipHeight: Dp,
    visiblePx: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Float>,
    loader: ThumbnailLoader,
    snapTargets: () -> List<Long>,
    snapThresholdMs: Long,
    onTrim: (clipId: String, trimStartMs: Long, trimEndMs: Long) -> Unit,
) {
    Row {
        val starts = project.clipStartTimesMs()
        project.clips.forEachIndexed { index, clip ->
            val clipStartPx = TimelineGeometry.msToPx(starts[index], pxPerMs)
            // key(): after a reorder each clip keeps its own state (drag offsets, tiles).
            key(clip.id) {
                // The selected clip's handles reach over its neighbours, so it's drawn on top.
                ClipView(
                    clip = clip,
                    clipStartMs = starts[index],
                    pxPerMs = pxPerMs,
                    height = clipHeight,
                    look = ClipLook(
                        selected = clip.id == selectedClipId,
                        multiSelected = clip.id in multiIds,
                        multiSelectMode = multiSelectMode,
                        soundOff = clip.muted || clip.volume == 0f || project.originalAudioMuted,
                        missing = clip.id in missingIds,
                    ),
                    visiblePx = (visiblePx.start - clipStartPx)..(visiblePx.endInclusive - clipStartPx),
                    loader = loader,
                    snapTargets = snapTargets,
                    snapThresholdMs = snapThresholdMs,
                    onTrim = { start, end -> onTrim(clip.id, start, end) },
                    modifier = Modifier.zIndex(if (clip.id == selectedClipId) 1f else 0f),
                )
            }
        }
    }
}
